title: Browns: Can HC Todd Monken break this unbelievable streak in Week 1?
summary: The Cleveland Browns hired Todd Monken as the franchise’s 19th full-time head coach at the end of January.  It was a smart move, as the 60-year-old Monken has considerable experience running an offense and is familiar with the AFC North Division after spending the past three seasons as offensive coordinator with the Baltimore Ravens. It […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 27: Head coach Todd Monken of the Cleveland Browns looks on prior to a preseason game against the New England Patriots at Huntington Bank Field on August 27, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns hired Todd Monken as the franchise’s 19th full-time head coach at the end of January. It was a smart move, as the 60-year-old Monken has considerable experience running an offense and is familiar with the AFC North Division after spending the past three seasons as offensive coordinator with the Baltimore Ravens. It is not without its risks, of course, as this will be Monken’s first shot at being a head coach at the NFL level, with his only previous head coaching experience coming at Southern Mississippi from 2013 to 2015. The Browns interviewed a variety of interesting candidates, but Monken was the preferred choice of owner Jimmy Haslam , and everything has always worked out when ownership has gotten involved in football decisions. Monken will get his first taste of being the head man in a game that counts when the Browns open the 2026 season against the Jacksonville Jaguars on September 13. It has been three years since the Browns won their opening game, a 24-3 defeat of the Cincinnati Bengals that saw quarterback Deshaun Watson pass and run for a touchdown in the victory. That won’t be the only streak that Monken will be looking to break, as the recent fate of Cleveland head coaches in their first game has been bleak. Would anyone be surprised to learn that Bud Carson was the last full-time head coach to win his Cleveland debut? And that came in 1989 in a 51-0 beatdown of the Pittsburgh Steelers? Since then, 11 full-time head coaches have come and gone in Cleveland, and not a single one kicked off their tenure with a victory. While we wait to see what Monken has in store for the Jaguars, let’s take a run through how each of Cleveland’s 18 full-time head coaches fared in their first game on the sidelines. Paul Brown – 1950 The NFL thought it was being clever when it scheduled the Browns to open the 1950 season on the road against the defending champion Philadelphia Eagles. Cleveland was coming off four years of dominance in the All-America Football Conference, and the Eagles were going to teach the upstarts a lesson. The Browns did not get the memo, however, and rolled to 448 yards of offense in a 35-10 victory that announced to the rest of the NFL that a new top dog was in town. Final record: 10-2 and the NFL Championship. Blanton Collier – 1963 In the first game in franchise history without Paul Brown as head coach, it was another blowout in the debut of the Blanton Collier tenure. Cleveland had 543 yards of offense, with Jim Brown combining for 262 rushing and receiving yards, as the Browns took down Washington by a score of 37-14. Final record: 10-4 and a Playoff Bowl loss to the Green Bay Packers. Nick Skorich – 1971 Another new head coach, another victory as the Browns opened their campaign under head coach Nick Skorich with a 31-0 win against the Houston Oilers. Quarterback Bill Nelsen led an effective offense, but it was a day for the defense as Cleveland held the Oilers to 35 rushing yards and forced six turnovers, including five interceptions. Final record: 9-5 and a Divisional Playoff loss to the Baltimore Colts. Forrest Gregg – 1975 All good things must come to an end, a lesson that Forrest Gregg learned in his first game as head coach of the Browns. Trailing 24-3 midway through the third quarter against the Cincinnati Bengals, Cleveland rallied behind a Gregg Pruitt touchdown run and a recovered fumble in the end zone by linebacker Charlie Hall to pull within seven points heading into the fourth quarter. The Browns threatened to tie the score, but two drives inside Cincinnati’s two-yard line ended up with zero points as the Bengals held on for the victory. Final record: 3-11, fourth place in the AFC Central Division. Sam Rutigliano – 1978 Sam Rutigliano was on the sidelines when the Browns opened the 1978 season at home against the San Francisco 49ers. Cleveland broke open a close game in the fourth quarter thanks to a 69-yard touchdown pass from Brian Sipe to Reggie Rucker, then closed out the scoring with a 23-yard field goal by Don Cockroft. Final record: 8-8, third place in the AFC Central Division. Marty Schottenheimer – 1985 Marty Schottenheimer took over as interim head coach midway through the 1984 season after Sam Rutigliano was fired, so this game serves as Schottenheimer’s first as the full-time head coach. And the game gave Cleveland fans a taste of the excitement to come in the next few years. The Browns rallied with 21 points in the fourth quarter, highlighted by Ozzie Newsome’s 25-yard catch-and-run touchdown to give Cleveland a seven-point lead with 38 seconds remaining against the St. Louis Cardinals. But the Cardinals used a 43-yard screen pass to Ottis Anderson to set up a game-tying touchdown to force overtime. St Louis won the toss in overtime, and then the game, as Neil O’Donoghue converted a 35-yard field goal. Final record: 8-8 and a Divisional Playoff loss to the Miami Dolphins. Bud Carson – 1989 In what was arguably the highlight of the Bud Carson era as a head coach, the Browns went into Pittsburgh in Week 1 and steamrolled the Steelers by a score of 51-0. Cleveland’s defense held Pittsburgh to 53 yards of total offense, sacked Pittsburgh quarterback Bubby Brister six times, and forced eight turnovers, three of which they turned into defensive scores. Final record: 9-6-1, with a loss in the AFC Championship Game to the Denver Broncos. Bill Belichick – 1991 It was a dreary start for the Browns under head coach Bill Belichick, as the offense managed only 32 rushing yards as Cleveland lost to the Dallas Cowboys by a score of 26-14. The Browns were trailing 13 points at halftime, but quickly cut into the deficit when Bernie Kosar hit Webster Slaughter on a 62-yard touchdown pass on the first play of the second half. The offense went cold from there, however, and the Cowboys closed out the scoring with a pair of field goals in the fourth quarter. Final record: 6-10, third place in the AFC Central Division. Chris Palmer – 1999 After three years without football, the Browns returned to the NFL to open the 1999 season at home on national television against the Pittsburgh Steelers in the first game under head coach Chris Palmer. There was no Hollywood ending, however, as the Browns managed just 40 yards of total offense, nine rushing yards, and two first downs in a 43-0 defeat. Final record: 2-14, sixth place in the AFC Central Division. Butch Davis – 2001 Points were hard to find in the first game under head coach Butch Davis. The game turned into a battle of field goals, with Phil Dawson’s 22-yarder tying the score at 6 with two minutes remaining. But a 49-yard kickoff return set up Seattle on the ensuing possession, and Rian Lindell converted a 52-yard field goal with three seconds remaining to leave the Browns on the wrong end of a 9-6 final score. Final record: 7-9, third place in the AFC Central Division. Romeo Crennel – 2005 It was another ugly day for the Browns in the debut of head coach Romeo Crennel, as the defense allowed 420 yards of total offense, and penalties wiped out a punt return touchdown and an interception return for a touchdown in what would be a 27-13 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. While Frisman Jackson posted the only 100-yard receiving game of his career, three turnovers from quarterback Trent Dilfer kept the offense from putting up a stronger fight. Final record: 6-10, fourth place in the AFC North Division. Eric Mangini – 2009 Cleveland took a three-point lead into halftime against the Minnesota Vikings thanks to a 67-yard punt return for a touchdown by Josh Cribbs, but it was all Vikings in the second half of a 34-20 loss in Eric Mangini’s first game as head coach. Cleveland had no answer for Minnesota’s…

The reality is that both of those things are probably the biggest storylines around the team and deserved the attention they received. While we are ready to move forward with Cleveland’s 2026 season, the decisions made this offseason undergird everyone’s expectations. If Garrett were still on the team, a solid veteran was starting at quarterback, the two exciting rookie wide receivers were on another team, and/or a young, inexperienced head coach was hired, Browns fans and media might see things differently heading into Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. A list of a few things I’m excited about and concerned about: Excited about HC Todd Monken’s Floor While no one can say for certain whether Monken will be in over his head as a head coach, I have no doubt that he will not be embarrassing Browns fans. For the first time in a long time, Cleveland has a coach with a ton of experience all over the NFL and college. While he’s a first-time head coach and could be fired within a year, I am confident he will not embarrass himself or the team, big picture. Concerned that the stepdown from Garrett to Verse uncovers many defensive deficiencies Garrett is the best player in the NFL, just ask the other players. His presence alone made Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham, Denzel Ward, Grant Delpit , and the rest of the defense better. Add on his performance, and it is possible that Browns defenders are not as good, and some may not even be close, as they’ve looked with Garrett with them. Verse is a darn good player, but the difference between good and game-changer can be stark. Excited about KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston AND… … Quinson Judkins, Harold Fannin Jr., and Isaiah Bond. I’m not sure the last time Cleveland had five offensive weapons that have either proven they are good players or clearly have the ability to do so. Bond might be the least productive, but his high end speed will help open things up for the rest of the Browns offense. Concepcion and Boston can be used in a variety of ways and have already made a lot of plays to start their careers. Just a lot of fun around a rebuilt offensive line and a mystery box of concern at quarterback. Concerned about the QB spot Why wouldn’t I be? Yes, an offense can be good running the ball and with a few key passes, but defenses that get to load the box can make things tough for Judkins and the rest of the running game. Whether it is Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel , or Taylen Green, the Browns offense could be handicapped and impact the development of the young players if the quarterback play is as bad or worse than last year’s. Excited about what is next for Graham and Schwesinger The Defensive Rookie of the Year outplayed Cleveland’s top pick (Graham) last year, but the defensive tackle really improved as the year went on. Very excited to see how those two young guys, along with Verse, Maliek Collins , and Quincy Williams , perform in the front seven in Year 2. Concerned about fan apathy The Browns have done very little, in fact, the opposite, to ingratiate themselves with the greatest fanbase in the world. The decision to start Watson added to that after his fan-blaming press conference, but Cleveland fans have slowly become apathetic toward their team. The Browns do not deserve support, but I am concerned that fans will miss out on the fun stuff because of the losing that has happened and could happen more this season. Excited about the upside, development of the Browns roster My favorite type of sports team is a championship-level team. After that is the young developing team with a lot of upside. Cleveland does not have the former but does have the latter, and I’m excited to share that with Browns fans who are able to push through even if the team is losing games. It really is one of the reasons I’m so excited for the SB Nation app, which I’ve said over and over again is all about bringing community together . Getting to talk about how we see the offensive line coming together, how those weapons on offense are playing well together and off of each other, how the defense is more creative and versatile, how “EMan” (Emmanuel McNeil-Warren) is being used, and, yes, the 2027 NFL draft helping complete the three-year rebuild are all things that are better when we get to talk about them together. I believe in the core of this team. I believe they have a chance to be decent to good this year, and I do believe they’ll be a fringe playoff contender in 2027. There is a bunch to be excited about, but the obvious concerns still linger. What are you excited about and concerned about heading into the 2026 Browns season? Join the conversation! Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There are so many unknowns about the Cleveland Browns going into next week’s season opener. How will HC Todd Monken do in the role for the first time at the NFL level ? What will the downturn from Myles Garrett to Jared Verse do to the defense? How will all the young roster players look in real games with fewer veterans around them? We do know that the Browns will need better quarterback play than they got last season from Joe Flacco, Dillon Gabriel, and Shedeur Sanders . While the NFL cycle may be moving away from huge passing numbers , last year’s performance was far from good enough. Taking a look at last year’s playoff teams for a reference point, the Los Angeles Rams led the NFL in passing yards with 4,557. On the low end of the 14 playoff teams were the following: Carolina Panthers – 3,048 Philadelphia Eagles – 3,303 Pittsburgh Steelers – 3,440 Given that the Panthers won the NFC South with a losing record at 8-9, they probably are not a good reference point for Cleveland, which has to deal with the more talented AFC North. (A note that not all playoff appearances are the same.) Last year, the Browns had the second-fewest passing yards in the NFL with 2,808 while the New York Jets were far behind with 2,385. Using the average of the Eagles and Steelers performances last year, Cleveland quarterbacks will need to throw for around 600 more yards this season. That is just 36 more yards a game, on average. Is passing yards the only indicator of passing game success? Of course not. Philadelphia and Pittsburgh combined for just 16 interceptions last year, while Cleveland quarterbacks gave away 18 of them while only throwing for 16 touchdowns. Also, the Detroit Lions had the third most passing yards in the NFL and still missed the playoffs. A lot has to happen for the Browns to have a shot at making the playoffs. Throwing for more yards, more touchdowns, and fewer interceptions is just a part of the equation. How many yards do you think the Browns will pass for in 2026? Join the conversation! title: Is the 5,000-yard QB extinct? Where Browns find themselves in the NFL’s cyclical nature
summary: There are always sayings in professional sports, even if they are not always backed up by data or film. Things like “low man wins” and “if it touches your hands, you should catch it.” Sometimes, jumping over someone works, and it takes an impressive effort to even get a finger on a pass, with catching […]
full_text: Sep 12, 2021; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) throws a pass as Cleveland Browns middle linebacker Anthony Walker (4) defends during the first half at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jay Biggerstaff-USA TODAY Sports There are always sayings in professional sports, even if they are not always backed up by data or film. Things like “low man wins” and “if it touches your hands, you should catch it.” Sometimes, jumping over someone works, and it takes an impressive effort to even get a finger on a pass, with catching it being impossible. The NFL has been a “head coach, offensive play caller, and quarterback league” for a while now. The Cleveland Browns hope they have the first two locked up with HC Todd Monken , but few believe that Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel , or Taylen Green fit the mold of a franchise-level quarterback. With the 2026 season about to kick off, Watson will get the first shot at proving pretty much everyone wrong . With college football’s Week 1 going into full swing on Saturday, many are already focused on what is expected to be a historic quarterback class. Will the Browns be bad enough, lucky enough, or package enough draft picks together to get the franchise guy in the 2027 NFL draft? Way too many things will happen between now and then for anyone to really know. The cyclical nature of the NFL calls into question whether the “coach, play caller, QB league” is still a truism. Between the first quarterback (Dan Marino) to throw for 5,000 yards and the next one (Drew Brees), 24 seasons took place without anyone reaching the mark. Since Brees’ 2008 season, 5,000-yard passing seasons have happened 13 times, but the last one was in 2002 (Patrick Mahomes). In the last two seasons, there were just six quarterbacks to throw for more than 4,000 yards. In an article on CBS Sports, Pete Prisco outlines five reasons “ the explosive NFL passing game has plummeted over the past decade ” and tries to answer “will it ever return?” The reasons all make sense, starting with shell coverage and creative defenses. That college systems are not developing offensive linemen or quarterbacks like they used to may never change, but coaches playing it safe can. The offensive coaches quoted in the piece believe they can find ways to be explosive again, but note that they will be much more difficult. Instead, the solution is part of the cycle of the NFL. More big bodies (13 personnel – 1 running back, 3 tight ends, 1 wide receiver) is something the Los Angeles Rams have already moved to. Redefining what an “explosive” passing play will be is also part of the process: “If I am going to throw the ball 40-45 yards down the field one-on-one, my quarterback has to put it in a perfect spot. That’s hard to come by. So find different ways to create explosives.” “It’s like a 20-yard in cut, so you bet your ass this is an explosive play now. Look at the defense. They are just sinking with no vertical threat. So if you want to throw a go-ball here, you can’t. So you attack the middle of the field as they get width. You take advantage of what you can win with and what I took away from our self scout was our quarterback’s good at throwing seams and ins, and he’s really good at it. So, with Cleveland currently void of certainty at the quarterback position, they’ll need a guy who can still control the game, make the big-time throws, and instill fear into the defense and confidence into his offensive teammates. Yet, with passing numbers coming down, do the Browns need to mortgage the future to find that guy, or should they try to get on the front edge of this cycle by building a complete roster while finding a quarterback along the way? After all, as one of our DBN Feed posters said, Cleveland fans always want the team to run the ball anyway: Do you think the NFL cycle is moving away from QB dependence? Do you think the Browns would be foolish to go all-in on a guy in the ‘27 NFL draft (assuming none of the current QBs light it up) given the passing trends? Join the conversation! title: Best-case scenario: Examining what could take the Cowboys to the next level
summary: If you could measure the level of excitement for the upcoming Dallas Cowboys season, it would be somewhere between 1.20 and 1.22 gigawatts. For those who slept through science class, that’s over a billion watts of excitement. It feels good, and it’s not lost on us that this team is coming off of two straight […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker (left) with head coach Brian Schottenheimer at training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If you could measure the level of excitement for the upcoming Dallas Cowboys season, it would be somewhere between 1.20 and 1.22 gigawatts. For those who slept through science class, that’s over a billion watts of excitement. It feels good, and it’s not lost on us that this team is coming off of two straight losing seasons. One might think, here we go again, typical Cowboys’ optimism despite not even considering if things didn’t go as planned. Not true. We’ve considered it and shared those particular unsettling items with you yesterday . Today, we bring you happier thoughts as we talk about what could happen if the stars line up just right for our beloved Cowboys. Parker is the real deal From the moment the defense steps on the field, all eyes will be on Christian Parker’s group. Promises of a new scheme have set high expectations for this unit. Obviously, things will be better, but mediocre is not the benchmark. For the Cowboys to be true contenders, the defense must find its way into the top 10 in efficiency. That means that fancy words like “multiple,” “gap-and-a-half,” and “Star” must deliver on their promises of confusing quarterbacks and creating opportunities for defenders to affect the play. No one expects things to be magically fixed overnight, but if the defense starts out of the gate with some noticeable improvements, that’s a good sign that things are trending in the right direction. The offense is hyper-efficient Being better on defense is crucial, but let’s be real. If this team is going places, it’s going to be because of the offense. In year two of Brian Schottenheimer and Klayton Adams, the offense is poised to continue their excellence. With a physical rushing attack and the best wide receiving duo in football, the table is set for good stuff. Concerns at tackle make some wonder if the offense has limitations, but the Cowboys’ scheme has already been dealing with that, and it hasn’t held them back. For this offense, the stars will shine as Dak Prescott has never had it this good with two monster playmaking receivers at his disposal. They have an all-hands-on-deck pass-blocking group that features excellent chip blocking from players like Brevyn Spann-Ford, Hunter Luepke, and Javonte Williams, although nobody much talks about that. The Cowboys have done something crafty. They have increased their floor by having all these security measures in place to protect Prescott, while still having the firepower to be absolutely explosive. In the end, this offense is poised for big things. The GOTI stuff is silly, but if the Cowboys come out of this season with the greatest offense of 2026, it will surprise no one. They have the tools to pull it off. Difference-making new guys Never have we had an offseason where fans have praised the Cowboys’ front office so much. All the shrapnel from the Micah Parsons trade has subsided as everyone is focused on all the new cars in the driveway. There is no guarantee that these new faces will deliver good things, but there’s a fair chance some will. Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark are great players. Any notion that their better days are behind them is completely dismissed, and they should be one of the most talented defensive tackle duos in the league, and that doesn’t even take into account third-wheel Otito Ogbannia, who has done nothing but quietly impress the coaches. But the trio in the back may be equally as impressive as the trio upfront. The new safety team of Caleb Downs, Jalen Thompson, and incumbent Malik Hooker offers the defense the most dynamic safety group this team has had in decades. And it doesn’t stop there. There’s a new trio of pass rushers added to the group with Rashan Gary, Malachi Lawrence, and Von Miller added to the rotation. New acquisition linebackers Dee Winters and Jaishawn Barham join the fun, and cornerback Cobie Durant is rarely mentioned simply because there are so many other guys to talk about. The Cowboys have thrown so many darts at fixing this defense that if just half of them stick, it’s going to lead to a huge turnaround for this unit. Schotty effect The jury is still out on the second-year head coach, but if all this culture stuff turns into something, this could finally be the key factor that helps this squad get over the divisional round hump. Schottenheimer has created the perfect emotional bedrock for a deep playoff run. He brings high levels of enthusiasm with a clear message that mistakes will be corrected, one way or another. He fosters trust and chemistry, insisting on a unified, high-morale football culture. If Schottenheimer is on to something, then just maybe, all the talent the Cowboys have rustled up will finally amount to something in January. It’s what’s held this team back in the past, and if they finally have the right coaches in the right places, this could be the factor that brings the Cowboys back to their championship ways. Can you think of anything else? What is something that could happen that could help the Cowboys be contenders again?

Depth Chart: DaRon Bland, Cobie Durant, Shavon Revel, Ameer Speed, Caelen Carson. Most Likely Addition: Former Eagles CB and current Free Agent, Adoree Jackson. Many have noted that former Wake Forest CB Caelen Carson is likely the 53rd man on the Dallas roster, meaning he is the weakest link/most likely to be replaced at some point this season. When Could Cowboys and Raiders Pull Off Blockbuster Maxx Crosby Trade? – Randy Gurzi, SI.com The Maxx Crosby rumors won’t die. As long as there is cap space, rumors of a big trade will persist. When could a Maxx Crosby trade actually happen? Parkins added that he doesn’t expect the trade to happen immediately, but instead believes Crosby will use the month of September as a sort of audition for interested teams. The five-time Pro Bowler had knee surgery this offseason and was originally traded to the Baltimore Ravens, but failed a physical. Parkins believes Crosby will use the first month of the year to show he’s healthy, which will lead to renewed trade talk, ultimately ending with Crosby wearing a Dallas uniform. Former Steelers HC Tomlin cites ‘intangibles’ for trading Pickens to Cowboys – Angel Torres, Cowboys Wire The Pittsburgh Steelers in hindsight look insane for giving up George Pickens for only a third-round pick. Ex-Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin further explaied the decision behind parting ways with the talented receiver. “For us, I just thought, it’s not only play, Tomlin said. “It’s development in other areas, intangible areas.” — Mike Tomlin on The Rich Eisen Show Those intangible qualities became especially important when the Steelers considered what Pickens would look like playing on a lucrative, second contract. Tomlin explained that big-money extensions come with responsibilities beyond producing statistics. Cowboys’ calculated risk to waive QB Joe Milton makes much more sense after latest intel on potential trade – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports The uproar over Milton’s release and subsequent return may have been triggered by the front office looking to make a move. Dolphins were interested in Milton or Howell Broaddus, who had previously indicated the Cowboys fielded calls for their quarterbacks prior to cuts on Sunday, revealed the Dolphins were one of those teams. “I was told that Miami was a team that were calling about your quarterbacks on Sunday,” Broaddus said on the show. “But they also traded for the guy in Green Bay (Kyle McCord). But Miami was a team that was calling.” This season may be defined by the first five weeks – RJ Ochoa, Blogging the Boys If the Cowboys stumble out of the gate to start the season, it’s going to be a big hurdle to overcome. Consider that through the first five weeks of the season the Cowboys: Play two games within the NFC East Immediately after have to go to Brazil For a “home” game against one of the AFC’s best Then return to travel for a game against another, maybe the NFL’s best defense Only to play at home on a short week againsta Buccaneers team that has been feisty as of late Games after this stretch include contests against the Packers, Eagles twice, Seahawks, and the Rams. The point here isn’t that the Cowboys are done with their most difficult opponents by Week 6. The point here is that the first wave of their marathon comes with more difficult circumstances that are out of their control in terms of travel and time.

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 8
summary: It is Day 8 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: Star-Telegram archive photo from Thanksgiving Day 1993. Dallas Cowboys' Leon Lett dives for a blocked fourth quarter field goal attempt as Bert Weidner of the Miami Dolphins scrambles for the ball Thursday, Nov. 25, 1993 in Irving , Texas. The live ball was recovered by Jeff Dellenbach of the Dolphins. Dolphins kicker Pete Stoyanovich then made the winning 19-yard field goal as time expired giving the Dolphins a 16-14 victory. It is Day 8 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. So here we go for Day 8 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit perhaps the strangest Thanksgiving game in Cowboys history. Played on an ice-covered Texas Stadium field, Dallas appeared to have secured the victory when Miami’s potential game-winning field goal was blocked. Then Leon Lett decided to make the mistake that gets replayed to this day. Thursday, November 25, 1993 Texas Stadium, Irving, Texas Final Score: Miami Dolphins 16, Dallas Cowboys 14 The defending Super Bowl champions entered at 7-3, while Miami was 8-2 despite losing Dan Marino to a season-ending Achilles injury. Conditions became the biggest storyline before kickoff. Freezing rain, snow and sleet covered the artificial turf, with the temperature around 32 degrees at kickoff and falling into the 20s. Players, officials and even kickers struggled to remain upright. Miami handled the conditions first. Keith Byars broke free for a 77-yard touchdown run during the opening quarter, giving the Dolphins a 7-0 advantage. Dallas responded in the second when Troy Aikman found rookie Kevin Williams for a four-yard touchdown to tie the game. Williams then produced the play that looked destined to become the lasting memory of the afternoon. With only 27 seconds remaining before halftime, he returned a punt 64 yards for a touchdown, navigating the frozen field before sliding through the end zone in celebration. Dallas went into halftime leading 14-7. The Cowboys never scored again. Pete Stoyanovich kicked field goals from 20 and 31 yards during the second half, gradually reducing Dallas’ advantage to 14-13. Emmitt Smith, still dealing with a bruised quadriceps suffered four days earlier, managed 51 rushing yards on 16 carries while adding nine catches for 46 yards. The conditions prevented Dallas from putting Miami away. Dallas still had an opportunity to create some breathing room late in the fourth quarter, but Eddie Murray missed a 32-yard field goal wide right. Miami took possession and drove into scoring range behind backup quarterback Steve DeBerg, including a crucial fourth-down completion to Byars that kept the possession alive. With Dallas leading 14-13 and only 15 seconds remaining, Stoyanovich lined up for a 41-yard field goal. Jimmie Jones penetrated the protection and blocked the kick. The football travelled beyond the line of scrimmage and came to rest on the frozen field. Under the rules, Dallas only needed to stay away from it and the Cowboys would take possession. Instead, Lett came charging toward the ball. As teammates desperately tried to keep everyone away, the 290-pound defensive tackle slid on the ice, touched the football and made it live again. Miami center Jeff Dellenbach recovered near the goal line with three seconds remaining. Stoyanovich was suddenly given a second opportunity. This time he converted from 19 yards, completing the extraordinary 16-14 Miami victory. Moments earlier, Dallas players and owner Jerry Jones had been celebrating what appeared to be a win. Now the Cowboys were walking off their own frozen field in disbelief. The lasting story, however, extends far beyond Lett’s mistake. Jimmy Johnson refused to blame the loss on one player and supported a devastated Lett afterward. The Cowboys responded exactly as a championship team would, they never lost again that season. Dallas won its next five regular-season games and all three postseason contests, finishing the run by going to Super Bowl XXVIII. This game belongs on the countdown because Cowboys history is filled with moments that became bigger than the final result. The sight of Lett sliding helplessly toward the football remains one of the most replayed Thanksgiving moments ever, but the response afterward says just as much about that Dallas team. The mistake could have fractured a contender. Instead, the Cowboys rallied around Lett and never lost again. #Cowboys vs #Dolphins 1993 Thanksgiving The Leon Lett Game Final Score: Miami Dolphins 16, Dallas Cowboys 14 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/V5aZdeHhwv — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) September 5, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Remarkably, this became the final loss of Jimmy Johnson’s five seasons as Cowboys head coach. title: This season may be defined by the first five weeks
summary: What is the most important and/or difficult stretch of the season for the Dallas Cowboys? Odds are we will feel differently about this. Historically and traditionally speaking, the answer tends to come later in the year. Late November, all of December, and the time into January gets hard as the marathon is coming to an […]
full_text: Aug 28, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer looks on during warm ups before the game against the New Orleans Saints at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What is the most important and/or difficult stretch of the season for the Dallas Cowboys? Odds are we will feel differently about this. Historically and traditionally speaking, the answer tends to come later in the year. Late November, all of December, and the time into January gets hard as the marathon is coming to an end with the playoffs on the horizon. This year though, let’s look at a different time. My very reckless stipulation that feels reasonable: If the Cowboys make it to Week 6 with four wins then they are going to the playoffs this season. Obviously the team reaching that mark would guarantee nothing, but these first five weeks present as the biggest challenge in this scenario. This isn’t necessarily the case because of who the Cowboys are playing. It is more of a result of the treacherous path that it entails from a travel and time perspective. Consider that through the first five weeks of the season the Cowboys: Play two games within the NFC East Immediately after have to go to Brazil For a “home” game against one of the AFC’s best Then return to travel for a game against another, maybe the NFL’s best defense Only to play at home on a short week againsta Buccaneers team that has been feisty as of late Games after this stretch include contests against the Packers, Eagles twice, Seahawks, and the Rams. The point here isn’t that the Cowboys are done with their most difficult opponents by Week 6. The point here is that the first wave of their marathon comes with more difficult circumstances that are out of their control in terms of travel and time. Those things are taxing and can impact contests. That isn’t breaking news. Maybe you disagree with this hypothesis. Maybe you feel a different stretch is more daunting for your own set of reasons. What is that stretch if so? Let us know in the comments below.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: How the Cowboys season could go wrong
summary: There is a lot of excitement heading into the new season for the Dallas Cowboys. Despite two straight losing seasons, some view them as contenders, that is, assuming their plan falls nicely into place. But what if things don’t? What if all the hope and optimism are replaced with despair and agony? Just how bad […]
full_text: There is a lot of excitement heading into the new season for the Dallas Cowboys. Despite two straight losing seasons, some view them as contenders, that is, assuming their plan falls nicely into place. But what if things don’t? What if all the hope and optimism are replaced with despair and agony? Just how bad could things get for this football team? While this is not a road anyone wants to meander down, it’s good to at least think about what could go wrong and evaluate if the Cowboys have a contingency plan. So, today, we’ll get a little dark and run through the hypotheticals that could lead to a complete collapse of the 2026 season. The unsettling Prescott pattern If the Cowboys lose their franchise quarterback for an extended amount of time, that’s bad news, and we’re all well aware of that. That means every year we hold our breath that Dak Prescott doesn’t get hurt. At 33 years old, he’s no longer a spring chicken, meaning his body doesn’t respond the same way, and certain ailments can linger. Over the last seven seasons, his availability has alternated between a healthy season and missing at least five games, including being lost twice with season-ending injuries. Should this pattern continue, it doesn’t bode well for the upcoming season, as he was fully healthy last season. No Dak in Dallas is the easiest way to take the air out of the season. Protecting Dak Keeping him healthy is of the utmost importance, but keeping him upright also matters. The Cowboys offense is in great shape with weapons galore, with one minor exception. Offensive tackles. There are huge concerns at both starting tackle positions. Left tackle Tyler Guyton has looked good in training camp, but he has dealt with injuries in each of his first two seasons. Right tackle Terence Steele has proven to be a liability at times, and it’s even been suggested that his job is up for grabs after the recent trade for Broderick Jones. And speaking of Jones, the former first-round tackle out of Georgia was sliding down the depth chart in Pittsburgh before the Cowboys swooped in and traded for him. While there are legit reasons to be excited about his upside, the current version of him leaves a lot to be desired, and the Cowboys could be in trouble if they had to rely on his services sooner rather than later. Whether it happens or not is a big unknown, but the team’s tackle position has the potential to be a giant disaster. Defensive learning curve For a defense that was as dreadful as it was last year, it’s a little strange to see so much optimism for this current group. The overhaul is real. Between the coaching staff and players, this is a completely different group, so drawing comparisons to the 2025 unit makes little sense. While the optimism is warranted, we must also understand that new defensive schemes don’t manifest into greatness overnight. There is an expected learning curve when a new coach shows up. A new philosophy with an influx of new components opens the door for communication breakdowns and blown assignments. The whole point of bringing Christian Parker in was to alleviate this, but there is no guarantee that it will work, and there’s a reasonable chance they’ll experience the typical growing pains early in the season. Not enough pass rush On paper, the Cowboys have done a lot to improve the team’s pass-rushing group. They’ve acquired two veterans, one via trade in Rashan Gary, and one in free agency in Von Miller. They have two young draft picks in Donovan Ezeiruaku and Malachi Lawrence. And they have one reclamation project in James Houston. These are fresh faces to the organization, as none of them had logged a single snap in a Cowboys uniform this time last year. It should be a fierce unit. But what if it’s not? What if Gary lives up to the billing that all those Green Bay Packers fans tried to warn us about? What if Miller plays like a regular 37-year-old pass rusher rather than one who defies Father Time? And what if the recent draft investments do not pan out? Potential stays potential until it develops into something else. The Cowboys appear to have their bases covered, not relying on a single individual thing to come through, but rather a collection of things, we have to consider the possibility that things don’t fall into place. Nothing will test raw defense quicker than repeated failures to put pressure on the quarterback. The rebound gang Every year, there’s new hope that a player lost to injury turns around and has a great season. Last year, it was a couple of Day 2 picks like Trevon Diggs and Sam Williams, who returned from injury, but added little to nothing to the team. Both are gone from the team. This year, the hope falls on two more Day 2 picks in Shavon Revel Jr. and DeMarvion Overshown. While their skills are very intriguing, we are waiting for them to erupt after proving to everyone that they are fully healthy. But that offers no promises. The possibility that more hiccups show up exists, and it could turn a positive into a negative. Additionally, we’re all expecting DaRon Bland’s left foot to be fully healed this time around, but if he runs into any setbacks, it could be much more strain on the Cowboys cornerback room, especially if the aforementioned Revel Jr. becomes more grabby than deflect-y. The Schottenheimer ruse That scene in the movie Step Brothers when they wear tuxedos to their job interview almost worked out when Seth Rogen was about to hire them. The dynamic of the interview changed abruptly (no spoilers), and the irony of the tuxedos suddenly turned into insanity. While everyone is enamored by the culture Brian Schottenheimer has created, nothing will change that faster than if the Cowboys stink it up on the football field. All his clichés, the backward visor, Sir Mix-a-lot press conference covers, or Greek dancing just won’t have the same feel to it if it doesn’t translate to winning. He’s a dad-joke coach, and while dads are loved, if fans don’t get what they want, they will run off screaming “I hate you!” and slam the door. These are all bad scenarios. If the Cowboys season breaks down, there’s a good chance a couple of these things happen. We’re all crossing our fingers that they avoid this type of mêlée, but we must at least look over the hill and be aware that such evil exists. Did we leave anything out? What is something that could go wrong and derail the Cowboys’ season?
author: Dan Rogers

title: Cowboys have struggled in recent season openers
summary: We have reached the single digits. There are now fewer than 10 days separating us from the 2026 season beginning for the Dallas Cowboys. This one kicks off on the road against the New York Giants in primetime, and the moment it begins everything we have thought about this team for most of the calendar […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - JANUARY 04: Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys and Jaxson Dart #6 of the New York Giants meet after the Giants beat the Cowboys 34-17 at MetLife Stadium on January 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images We have reached the single digits. There are now fewer than 10 days separating us from the 2026 season beginning for the Dallas Cowboys. This one kicks off on the road against the New York Giants in primetime, and the moment it begins everything we have thought about this team for most of the calendar year is suddenly subject to change both positively and negatively. It is only one game, but the season opener can often feel bigger than that. If your team wins it then they have started stacking things together. That is one fewer win necessary to reach certain points like double-digits or securing the division. You get the picture. This year the Cowboys have a more-important-than-normal game to start the season as it is against a division rival. The Giants have been a bit moribund for a decade now, but that doesn’t change the significance and weight of this being an NFC East matchup. What’s more, it is one of three that Dallas plays on the road across the season at large. It isn’t hyperbole to say that a win would be huge. Given potential tiebreakers down the road that is objectively undeniable. Unfortunately for the Cowboys they have a rather meek record in their last 10 season openers, coincidentally (and nicely for symmetry’s sake) this now encompasses the entire Dak Prescott era as he started all of these games. Last 10 Dallas Cowboys season openers 2025: Loss at Philadelphia Eagles 2024: Win at Cleveland Browns 2023: Win at New York Giants 2022: Loss vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers 2021: Loss at Tampa Bay Buccaneers 2020: Loss at Los Angeles Rams 2019: Win vs. New York Giants 2018: Loss at Carolina Panthers 2017: Win vs. New York Giants 2016: Loss vs. New York Giants Now fortunately for the Cowboys, 75% of their four wins in this span came against the G-Men specifically. They did lose one though, the first start that Dak ever made (why didn’t Terrance Williams get out of bounds?). Also, nothing about what happened in any of these season-openers has anything to do with, for the most part, who the 2026 Cowboys are. This is an entirely different team, and that goes for the Giants as well. In fact this is arguably the most unpredictable Giants team that the Cowboys have faced throughout the Prescott era where they have dominated their rivals. Dallas did see Jaxson Dart in last year’s season finale, but that was a meaningless game as both teams were already eliminated from playoff contention. Plus, John Harbaugh is now in tow as well. Whatever the case, hopefully the Cowboys can rip off a win and get things started on the right foot. Most people believe they will. But what most people believe is hardly ever a guarantee.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: Quinnen Williams sees growth in the Cowboys defense
summary: Quinnen Williams arrived in Dallas halfway through a defensive disaster, but his seven games in Dallas did little to change the trajectory of a defense that had already gone badly off the rails. Nine months later, Williams sees something very different. “The growth, it’s like night and day,” Williams said of the strides made by […]
full_text: Quinnen Williams arrived in Dallas halfway through a defensive disaster, but his seven games in Dallas did little to change the trajectory of a defense that had already gone badly off the rails. Nine months later, Williams sees something very different . “The growth, it’s like night and day,” Williams said of the strides made by the Cowboys on the defensive side of the ball, and in such a short period of time. “Starting in OTAs, and starting the first week of training camp, getting a chance to go against one of the best offenses in battle every single day has helped us tremendously. The mindset coming from the coaches, top down to the players and to the leadership, has been drastically changed. It’s just fun, man.” “It’s been amazing — from where we started off in OTAs to where we are at now,” he explained. “We’ve got some fine tuning, some things to clean up, some things to do, but I feel comfortable. The progressions that we made, the growth and the development that we have made, and to go into the right direction that we wanted to go into.” There are several reasons for that change. The Cowboys brought in Christian Parker and a modernized defensive scheme. They also surrounded the new coordinator with considerably more talent, trading for Rashan Gary and Dee Winters, acquiring Jalen Thompson, Cobie Durant, P.J. Locke, and Von Miller in free agency, and added talent via the draft with the likes of Caleb Downs, Malachi Lawrence, and Jaishawn Barham. And then there is the daily competition. Williams compared the experience to his time at Alabama, when he was constantly going against future first-round picks. Only now, he says, the competition is even better. “The last time I kind of felt this was when I was at ‘Bama, when it came down to you going against first-rounders across from you,” he said. “But here in the NFL, it’s All-Pros everywhere, getting a chance to go against one of the best offenses in the league and one of the best quarterbacks in the league. “And we’ve got one of the best offensive lines in the league, so using them as a helping tool to get better every single day, and the urgency level from a defensive standpoint to get better every single day. It’s been well-needed and fun. It’s definitely a battle.” A new defensive coordinator, a revamped roster, and an elite offense providing daily competition. Williams sees the difference. But notice what he doesn’t say. He doesn’t say the Cowboys have arrived. He doesn’t say the defense is fixed. He doesn’t even say they’re good. Instead, he says: “I just can’t wait to see the process and the results from all the hard work, but we’re not done yet.” That’s probably the most important part of everything Williams had to say. The pieces are in place. Whether they fit together remains to be seen. We’ll find out more in the season opener against the Giants.
author: One Cool Customer

title: Cowboys news: Von Miller is ‘living a dream’ in Dallas
summary: Von Miller was a big addition to the Cowboys during the offseason, and he couldn’t be happier to be back in Texas. Tyler Guyton is entering the most important season of his young career, and his play, or lack thereof, will have a lot to do with how Dallas performs on offense. Joe Milton was […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 28: Von Miller #40 of the Dallas Cowboys walks off the field after the 2026 NFL preseason game against the New Orleans Saints at AT&T Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images Von Miller was a big addition to the Cowboys during the offseason, and he couldn’t be happier to be back in Texas. Tyler Guyton is entering the most important season of his young career, and his play, or lack thereof, will have a lot to do with how Dallas performs on offense. Joe Milton was brought back on the practice squad, and according to Dak Prescott, it gives the quarterback room a boost. Camden Brown has taken full advantage of his opportunities, but his main impact this year likely won’t be as a wide receiver. Von Miller on looming debut for the Cowboys: ‘My smile is back’ – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com Von Miller has been in the NFL for a decade and a half and has had tremendous success. However, being back in Texas and playing for the Cowboys is something that means a lot to him. “[The media is] probably the 50th person to tell me that,” said the eight-time Pro Bowler. “The smile has come back, you know? I’ve always loved playing football. I’ve been able to play for some amazing teams, with amazing quarterbacks and amazing coaches. But it’s just something different about being here. … Coming here to The Star and seeing this amazing facility, and going to the stadium, I am glad we had that preseason game because I was in awe.” Why did the Dallas Cowboys choose Sam Howell over Joe Milton III? – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram Joe Milton is back in Dallas on their practice squad after losing the QB2 battle to Sam Howell. However, the reason the latter won out isn’t too surprising. One of the more debated topics of the roster moves around the NFL over the past week was the Dallas Cowboys’ decision to waive backup quarterback Joe Milton III in favor of keeping Sam Howell on the 53-man roster to be the primary backup to Dak Prescott. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer explained that the decision to keep two quarterbacks was likely always going to be the case to preserve roster spots at other positions. While three quarterbacks made the initial 53-man roster , Milton was waived a day later to make room for running back Emari Demercado . Cowboys add veteran tight end to practice squad – Connor Livesay, Blogging The Boys The Cowboys have being a lot of wheeling and dealing lately. On Thursday, they added veteran tight end James Mitchell. After a nail-biting 24 hours waiting to see if quarterback Joe Milton would clear waivers and return to the practice squad, the Dallas Cowboys are not done adding to it. The team announced late on Thursday that they have signed veteran tight end James Mitchell to their practice squad. Mitchell started his career in Detroit after being selected in the fifth round of the 2022 NFL Draft out of Virginia Tech. 2026 NFL season X factors: Key players for all 32 teams – Ben Solak, ESPN There’s a lot of buzz about the Cowboys offense going into this season, especially with George Pickens being back. However, Tyler Guyton is the pivotal piece. Guyton has the physical tools of a quality starting left tackle, but he has suffered mental lapses and taken easy penalties. Since he entered the league in 2024, Guyton is third among tackles in penalties per game (0.84). He has missed time because of ankle, shoulder and knee injuries. Now, he needs to string together consistent, mistake-free play. A leap from Guyton would benefit the entire offensive line. Guyton and right tackle Terence Steele warrant some chip help in pass protection, but it’s hard to cater to both sides of the line. Dak Prescott Shares What Joe Milton Return Means To Cowboys – Randy Gurzi, SI.com Dak Prescott has built a relationship with Joe Milton since he came to Dallas in a trade last year. Now that he’s back on the practice squad, Prescott expressed what having him back means. “It means a lot. Just me, personally, I thought he would’ve been picked up in the waivers or whatever it is. Fortunate for us, we got a hell of a player back and a guy that makes our room better, a guy that makes our team better. His spirit, just the way that he approaches the day, he’s a hell of a dude, he’s a hell of a competitor, one of the best at throwing the ball, honestly, and just his talent. Just the way he’s jumped and progressed from year to year, I know what’s ahead of him,” Prescott said via Jon Machota of The Athletic . Mailbag: How much will Brown contribute? – Nick Eatman, DallasCowboys.com Wide receiver Camden Brown has been a fan favorite during training camp and the preseason, and people were ecstatic that he made the final roster. However, the expectations for him need to be realistic. Now, if he shows the ability to play well on special teams and he’s valuable enough to take to the game and maybe play a little on offense, then let’s see it. But my guess is that he’ll probably be inactive for a lot of this season. And there’s nothing wrong with that. I saw Miles Austin sit for a few years before finally making a huge splash in Year 4. And think about Ryan Flournoy was barely a factor for two years and now he’s WR3 who won’t play much special teams at all. Daily discussion question: What is your biggest concern for the Giants game?
author: Matthew Lenix

title: Broncos need a consistent running game to take the next step in 2026
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! The Denver Broncos offense has the potential to be really dangerous this season. The Broncos have the quarterback and the offensive line, and have finally added an offensive weapon in Jaylen Waddle. There’s the emergence of second-year receiver Pat Bryant. Plus, you have a new playcaller, Davis Webb, thrown into the […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 06: J.K. Dobbins #27 of the Denver Broncos runs the ball during an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Empower Field at Mile High on November 6, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! The Denver Broncos offense has the potential to be really dangerous this season. The Broncos have the quarterback and the offensive line, and have finally added an offensive weapon in Jaylen Waddle. There’s the emergence of second-year receiver Pat Bryant. Plus, you have a new playcaller, Davis Webb, thrown into the mix. But for Denver’s offense to reach that potential, it starts and stops with the running game. The Broncos must have a consistent and effective run game in 2026. If that happens, it opens so much for Nix and Webb. It’ll make Denver that much harder to defend. It’s the consistency that’s the biggest key. When asked about the running game and consistency this week, Broncos head coach Sean Payton said: “I think part of that was health last year when we lost (RB) J.K. (Dobbins). We had a young backfield. That all kind of leads to the things that help teams win: time and possession, playing good defense. These things are tied together. They’re not, ‘Vance (Joseph) and Davis, go do your thing.’ There’s a lot more to winning each week in regard to how we’re going to win this game and what we think we have to do to win this game. “So, per our run game, there’s some really good things I think that we’re doing. Then, ultimately, you kind of settle in on what type of run team you are relative to a zone scheme, a gap scheme, and those types of things. So we certainly feel like we’re further along than we’ve been here in my three years, just with the depth in both groups.” Of course, it’ll help if Dobbins stays healthy. When he’s on the field, he’s one of the better running backs in the NFL. Yet even if Dobbins misses some time, the Broncos have depth at the position. RJ Harvey is a year older, and Jonah Coleman seems like the real deal. That not only helps with the consistency but also the confidence. Webb and Payton know they have the guys to be effective, regardless of what happens. It also helps that Denver returns basically the whole offense from a season ago. That means the players know the system and what they need to do to have success. “I think just the understanding of what techniques we’re trying to apply on which plays, which looks, which leverages,” Broncos right tackle Mike McGlinchey said to the media this week. “Just kind of honing in on that. We had a pretty good grasp of all that before, and like I said earlier, we’ve done it a long time together. “Switching a couple of the techniques in and out depending on the scheme or the play or whatever it is, I think we’ve done a good job. It’s been a great camp. Our group is ready to go, and I’m excited to see where we can go as the season unfolds.” If the Broncos get a consistent and effective running game this season on offense, watch out. Horse Tracks
author: Ian St. Clair

title: Sean Payton comments on Broncos’ focus competing in a ‘real good’ division
summary: The regular season is literally just days away and the Denver Broncos are trying to follow up a 14-3 season with one that matches or beats it. The challenge is significant. Of the 36 teams who have won 14 or more games in a regular season, only two (’89 49ers and ‘03 Patriots) have won […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 28: Head Coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos walks on the sidelines during the second quarter against the Minnesota Vikings in a preseason game at Empower Field at Mile High on August 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The regular season is literally just days away and the Denver Broncos are trying to follow up a 14-3 season with one that matches or beats it. The challenge is significant. Of the 36 teams who have won 14 or more games in a regular season, only two (’89 49ers and ‘03 Patriots) have won at least that many games the following season . To make things even more difficult, the Broncos are playing in an AFC West that is considered to be stacked with talent this season. Head coach Sean Payton said that now that they’ve won the AFC west they must find a way to stay there. “There’s a history with all those division opponents and usually you have to find a way to beat the one that’s at the top,” Payton said this week. “So that was our task right away, it was Kansas City. They had won this division however many years in a row… We’re competing in a real good division. You just look around, everyone has gotten better. The focus more is internal, our improvement and playing well.” So while it would be great to see Denver win another 14 games this season, it isn’t necessary to take care of business in their division. Win the division first. Then worry about playoff seeding. A lot must go right for a 14+ win season, but you don’t need a 14+ win season to in titles. Horse Tracks
author: Tim Lynch

title: Discussion: What are you most looking forward to seeing in Lions vs. Saints?
summary: We’re officially just a week away from the Detroit Lions’ season opener against the New Orleans Saints. Our long wait is almost over, and it will be a joy just to have the NFL back in our lives. But now that we’re within striking distance of Week 1, it’s time to actually start thinking about […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 23: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions runs in action against the New York Giants at Ford Field on November 23, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re officially just a week away from the Detroit Lions’ season opener against the New Orleans Saints. Our long wait is almost over, and it will be a joy just to have the NFL back in our lives. But now that we’re within striking distance of Week 1, it’s time to actually start thinking about the game. The Lions may be considered relatively big favorites—6.5 points according to FanDuel—but the first week of the season can be goofy. Teams tend to both be unpredictable and sloppy to kick off the season, and the Saints may not be too bad this year. It’s easy to forget that they finished the season winning four of their last five games. And we have no idea what the Lions are going to look like either? What will the reformed offensvie line look like? What will offensvie coordinator Drew Petzing have up his sleeve? Will Detroit’s front seven be as good as they looked in training camp? So today’s Question of the Day is: What are you looking forward to seeing the most in Lions vs. Saints? My answer: Well, outside of EVERYTHING, I’m excited to watch Jahmyr Gibbs. This offseason, Gibbs’ reputation seems to have launched into top-three running back conversation. What’s interesting about that rise in popularity is that it comes after a pretty mediocre season. By rushing success rate, Gibbs was just 25th out of 48 qualifying running backs. By EPA per rush, he was just 17th. But, of course, much of Gibbs’ struggles were caused by offensive line issues. Now, if you look at rushing yards over expected, Gibbs finished seventh in the NFL, per NFL Pro, and that’s what makes him extremely exciting to watch every game. Even if the Lions’ offensive line struggles out of the gate again this year, Gibbs is a danger to make a big play anyways. The offensive line could struggle to create a hole on 20 out of 21 plays. But on that one play? Gibbs could make a house call from 80 yards away. On top of that, I get the feeling we’ll finally start to see him expand his game a little as a true receiver—and more Gibbs with the ball in his hands is a good thing. What’s something specific you’re looking forward to in next week’s Lions season opener? Share your thoughts in the comment section below. Join the conversation! title: Detroit Lions fans pick favorite for RB2 role
summary: Earlier this week, we published our latest SB Nation Reacts survey, sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook, and asked Detroit Lions fans: Which Lions RB will get the majority of Isiah Pacheco’s snaps? While Jahmyr Gibbs is going to be the clear RB1/“bell cow” back, the loss of Pacheco to injured reserve has raised questions […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions running back Jacob Saylors (25) runs the ball against the Washington Commanders in the second quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Earlier this week, we published our latest SB Nation Reacts survey, sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook , and asked Detroit Lions fans: Which Lions RB will get the majority of Isiah Pacheco’s snaps? While Jahmyr Gibbs is going to be the clear RB1/“bell cow” back, the loss of Pacheco to injured reserve has raised questions about who will take on his reps. While giving those reps to Gibbs is an easy solution, the Lions won’t want to overload their superstar and will need to keep him fresh. That’s likely why over 90% of the fan base debated between Sione Vaki and Jacob Saylors stepping into a larger role. The results of the vote are in: Saylors started all three preseason games and looked steady and consistent in doing so. He showed a lot of technical skills and was productive, even though he often worked behind the reserve offensive line. Let’s take a closer look at the comment section of our original article and The Feed post to see fans’ explanations for selecting Saylors (lightly edited for clarity). grimy0185 : “I think it will become clear pretty early on that Saylors is RB2 with or without Pacheco on the active roster.” Prof_SJR : “Would hope Vaki has progressed to the point where he is RB2, but he is also highly valued on special teams. Seems like Saylors has shown better pure RB skills.” Lions86 : “Ultimately, I think Saylors will be RB2; he is just more of a natural running back, and he can catch the ball out of the backfield too. It might come down to who can block in the backfield best.” While most fans’ votes landed on Saylors, this is a week in which my opinion doesn’t align with the majority. Saylors looked solid in the preseason, but unless fans were at training camp, they never got to see the steps Vaki has taken on offense because he didn’t play in the preseason. Some of that was due to injury, but the coaches also stepped in and kept him out of situations. What fans may have missed is that Vaki has consistently run as RB2 while Pacheco has been out, and his skill set gives him opportunities to find the field. While Saylors is experienced, balanced, and reliable, Vaki is bigger and has shown enough power to produce in short-yardage situations; he is also a former receiver with the hands to match, but what will get him on the field more than anything else is likely pass protection. Vaki is an ELITE pass protector, and that will allow the Lions to put him on the field in any situation. Here are a few Vaki supporters from the comment sections (lightly edited for clarity). ULTIMATEpunisher007 : “I do think it’s Vaki. It’s not just running the ball but also pass blocking. As an RB, you have to be confident in picking up the blitz and protecting your QB. I think Dan will trust Vaki in that role to protect Goff before Saylors. He’s basically acting as the personal protector for the QB.” Waitingsince57 : “The coaching staff “seems” to trust Vaki WAY more than the fan base. They see him every day in practice, where we have hardly ever seen him in action due to his injuries. Saylors performed great in the preseason but not against NFL starters. Coaches will decide, and I think it will be Vaki.“ JohnLion777 : “Next man up. And like it or not, at this moment, that man is Vaki. title: Discussion: Which Detroit Lions player is under the most pressure in 2026?
summary: Earlier this week, ESPN put out a list of the players and coaches most under pressure for the 2026 NFL season. No Detroit Lions made their list, but it certainly got me thinking. This season is a big one for the Lions organization. Last year was their first significant step back under general manager Brad […]

Reed (4) during pregame introductions prior to the Detroit Lions versus the Pittsburgh Steelers game on Sunday December 21, 2025 at Ford Field in Detroit, MI. (Photo by Steven King/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Earlier this week, ESPN put out a list of the players and coaches most under pressure for the 2026 NFL season . No Detroit Lions made their list, but it certainly got me thinking. This season is a big one for the Lions organization. Last year was their first significant step back under general manager Brad Holmes and coach Dan Campbell, and the voices of the dissenters and doubters are starting to grow in volume. Whispers of the Lions’ “window being closed” are suddenly a little more audible, and some are openly questioning whether the franchise will slide back to “same old Lions.” Now, most of that is pure nonsense after one failed season. And if history is any indication, this era of Lions football thrives the most when the doubters are the loudest. Still, there’s certainly a lot of pressure on this regime to compete and succeed this year. Let’s put aside the obvious pressure on Holmes and Campbell and talk about specific players. Which Lions player is under the most pressure in 2026? My answer: Because of the failures of the 2024 NFL Draft class, I think there’s a ton of pressure from the 2025 draft class to become young tentpoles of the franchise, and a Year 2 jump would do wonders for this team. If Tate Ratledge can continue his progression and become a great-to-elite guard, it would help out rookie right tackle Blake Miller and Detroit’s center issues. If Tyleik Williams continues to be a strong run defender and adds on some pass rush juice, this defensive line has a chance to be really special. If Isaac TeSlaa can add yet another weapon to Detroit’s passing offense arsenal, there may be no defense that can stop them. And if Ahmed Hassanein can continue his impressive training camp, Detroit may have a defensive line rotation that would rival what the Seahawks had last year. Outside of the 2025 draft class, there is going to be a lot of pressure on the left guard and center positions to make sure the offensive line returns to form. D.J. Reed needs to play at a CB1 level and stay healthy to help answer some serious questions at the cornerback position. And Derrick Barnes needs to step up and justify Detroit’s investment in him a few years ago. Which other Lions players do you think are under the most pressure this season? Smith has incentives in his deal to reach $16.25 million, and he’s expected to be on the field for Brian Flores’ defense against the Packers next Sunday. title: Weekend Musings: Some Houston Texans thoughts before the regular season
summary: Only 2 QBs total on the entire roster? The roster churn in the post-cutdown chaos is effectively over. Houston has its 53-man roster and 16-man practice squad situated. Yet, among all of the players that can call Houston their team, the squad will only have 2 active QBs (Stroud, Mills), and as of this writing, […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - AUGUST 28: Head coach DeMeco Ryans of the Houston Texans looks on during the first half of a preseason game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Only 2 QBs total on the entire roster? The roster churn in the post-cutdown chaos is effectively over. Houston has its 53-man roster and 16-man practice squad situated. Yet, among all of the players that can call Houston their team, the squad will only have 2 active QBs (Stroud, Mills), and as of this writing, ZERO QBs on the practice squad. The primary reason for that situation is that presumed QB3 Graham Mertz suffered a season-ending ACL tear in the 1st preseason game. QB Brett Rypien was called off the couch to play in Houston’s final two preseason games, but not 48 hours after his final play (strip-sack fumble), Rypien was gone. Granted, a QB3 is not usually the highest depth priority for a team. With Houston, depth pieces along the lines, defense and special teams ability dictated much of their personnel actions. While the Texans likely have a list of QB names they can call should the need arise to get an arm on the roster during the season, said player will likely be at more of a disadvantage if they take live snaps. Being a backup is hard enough, but it is that much harder if you are just trying to learn the playbook and lingo, to say nothing of diagnosing a complicated NFL defense. With Mertz on IR for the season, Houston might have at least considered one QB to store on the practice squad to have some familiarity with the system. Especially when you factor that Stroud has missed games in 2 of his 3 seasons due to concussions, Mills might have to play some games. If Mills is the sole QB option after Stroud, that can be a lot of risk for a team, even with a defense like Houston’s. Watch the O-line…again. Hasn’t that been the cry of this team for years? Fix the Oline. This offseason, Caserio used free agency and the draft (once again) to fortify that position. Yet, the projected starting Oline for Sept 13 has three holdovers from last season, and the two big free agent signings as either second string (Wyatt Teller at LG) or on IR (Braden Smith at RT). 1st round pick Keylan Rutledge at least locked down a spot at LG, but the enduring image of that so far was him getting planted on a play that went to the other side of the field. Neal Brown, a bargain-bin pickup, at least locked down the C position. Granted, when we did see the starting Oline in limited action in the preseason, they moved the ball fairly effectively. Will that be the case against Buffalo? Unfortunately, we will have to wait to see if this will work. The NFL to NCAA pipeline? If nothing else, college football’s “official” kickoff this weekend, along with the NFL starting next week, should drive a lot of the crazy non-playing stories further back in the sports pages. Yet, of all the crazy, the idea of NFL players returning to college to play football might be the looniest plotline out there. Then again, loony might be reality when Clemson kicks off against LSU this Saturday, when players that were in NFL training camps but days ago might suit up to play for LSU. Yes, there is a lot more to the story, between the clumsiness and ineffectiveness of the NCAA, the increasing role of judge-shopping to obtain a favorable ruling for a player and the financial incentives of the NIL era vs. salaries of NFL practice squad/back-of-the-depth chart players. No player that was in Texans training camp is involved in this situation at this point. Hopefully, this will die out after this season when the new NCAA eligibility rules kick in but talk about something that wasn’t on the bingo card to start the year. View Link Positive Reviews for the Rivalry Uniforms: In the never-ending quest for NFL teams to make more money to have something new and fresh for the fans, the Texans issued their “Rivalry” uniforms. Likely some of you have bought them, which Texans players will sport for games against rivals, like the Week 11 game vs. the Colts. While social media is mixed on the uniforms, “neutral” sports media sites are high on the new uniforms. That it is an homage to Houston car culture is a nice touch. Would it be better with more Columbia Blue? Of course. Then again, there is a rather, uh, colorful history about that color…one that is likely not disappearing anytime soon. Stroud Contract: Looks like Stroud is gambling on himself this season. After a series of back-and-forth media announcements, it seems clear that no new contract will get signed between the Stroud and the Texans before the start of the regular season. Based on various reports, Houston looked to offer Stroud ~$50M/year, keeping him well within the top 12 of QB salaries. Stroud’s camp was supposedly looking between $60M-$70M. Sometimes, such a bet can pay off (see Flacco, Joe in 2012). Then again, when you gamble, there is always a chance to lose. A promotion for a (former) Texan: Last season, JJ Watt was a full-time color analyst for CBS. On the #2 team with long-time broadcaster Ian Eagle, he got the chance to offer a D-Lineman perspective. Generally, the reviews were positive, especially as he wasn’t meant to be the face of the sports broadcast team for CBS. However, this past month, the man in the #1 color analyst spot, Tony Romo, was arrested for OWI in Wisconsin. CBS effectively suspended him indefinitely, leaving an opening for the #1 spot. What CBS’ long-term plans are for that spot, we don’t entirely know. Romo was not exactly in great standing over the past couple of years. However, the tandem of Eagle-Watt is being broken up, with Watt now taking the #1 analyst spot. Perhaps it helps that Watt isn’t a total TV rookie, but will CBS rue breaking up a fairly effective team? Also, we don’t know if Watt will cover that many Texans’ games, since he will be likely at the marquee/late-afternoon games. While Houston is good, they don’t usually get the 3:25 Central time slots on Sunday. This might hurt in another way. Houston was 4-0 in games Watt called last season. Just a few thoughts in the last week before our emotional well-being get dictated by the on-field performance of the Texans. Until then…
