title: Rams can remain buyers into the season
summary: At best, the Los Angeles Rams have a 15% chance to win the Super Bowl. That percentage is higher than any of the other 31 teams. Still, I wouldn’t exactly bet my house on a probability that usually feels remote. The problem is that the Rams have set themselves up for a championship or failure […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 25: Davante Adams #17 of the Los Angeles Rams catches a pass in front of Josh Jobe #29 of the Seattle Seahawks during the third quarter in the NFC Championship game at Lumen Field on January 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) | Getty Images At best, the Los Angeles Rams have a 15% chance to win the Super Bowl . That percentage is higher than any of the other 31 teams. Still, I wouldn’t exactly bet my house on a probability that usually feels remote. The problem is that the Rams have set themselves up for a championship or failure season. Anything short of the Lombardi Trophy will be a disappointment. In a league where attrition and parity are two of the strongest and unseen forces, the team may as well be attempting to land on the moon. In some ways the sky-high expectations may also be a good thing for fans. Les Snead, Sean McVay, and the Rams understand the mission: win a Super Bowl in 2026. That means if LA loses a piece here or there or the roster isn’t meshing as well as expected, you can bet Snead will pick up the phone to remedy the issue. The Rams have their quarterback of the future, one we feel especially good about after a highly efficient preseason showing. They can remain aggressive for 2026 because they have security thereafter. Where could Snead and the team make tweaks in order to keep this locomotive on the tracks? Let’s take a look. Offensive tackle Simply put, this probably isn’t happening. It’s still worth mentioning on this list because the depth is concerning . I’m not discounting the selection of Ty Simpson when I say this, but the Rams had options at tackle in the first round of this spring’s draft. They opted for future security instead of shoring up a position that was not deep. For example, the Lions drafted Blake Miller four picks after Simpson. The Panthers selected Monroe Freeling two spots later. Max Iheanachor was taken by the Steelers two slots after that. Would the Rams have maximized value if they dipped into this middle to late first round pool? Probably not, but teams draft for need all the time. And if you expect another franchise to trade away a starting level player mid-season, there’s no way it’s happening. We almost never see quality tackles move teams in the middle of the year. You can do it, but the types of players that are available usually invoke some buyer’s remorse. The Rams have made their bed at offensive tackle. They now must lie in it. Receiver Assuming they remain healthy and off the league’s disciplinary radar, Puka Nacua and Davante Adams form a strong receiver duo. Those are big ifs, however. I don’t love LA’s receiving depth behind the big two. The Rams told us they don’t either by the fact they kept seven players at the position in a year they are expected to put more tight ends on the field than they ever have—plus the late trade acquisition of Tutu Atwell. Terrance Ferguson figures to be the de facto WR#3. And then there is the long-term questions at receiver. Will Nacua receive a contract extension and return in 2027? Adams is near the end of the career and this is likely his last season in LA, especially if they make good on their championship hopes. Adding to this room wouldn’t be difficult. We see receivers traded ahead of the league’s deadline every year. They can also make an impact on relatively short acclimation periods with their new team, including how the Rams added Odell Beckham back in 2021. These are some names I would keep an eye on if LA needs more firepower: Rashod Bateman, Ravens Brian Thomas, Jaguars Troy Franklin, Broncos Skyy Moore, Packers (punt return option) Jordan Addison, Vikings Quarterback Stetson Bennett and Ty Simpson are more like 2A and 2B as the backups to Matthew Stafford, but do the Rams really trust either one to step in this season given the thin margins the team is working against? The most secure solution if Stafford misses extended time is to phone Jimmy Garoppolo, who is currently a free agent and reconsidering his offseason retirement. It wouldn’t take much future capital in order to bring back someone like Garoppolo. It’s still a reasonable possibility and worth keeping on the radar. Cornerback LA is dangerously short-handed at corner. They really only have two trustworthy players at the position: Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson. Fans will likely see more of Emmanuel Forbes than they are expecting and probably want, at least until we find out how the Rams ultimately use McDuffie. If he plays inside often, Forbes is effectively a starting perimeter corner for this team. That is a position that could easily be upgraded, and LA may be walking a thin line after seemingly fixing their Achilles heel from last season. These are some names to consider later in the year: JuJu Brents, Dolphins Christian Gonzalez, Patriots (in contract dispute) Joey Porter, Steelers (in contract dispute) Riley Moss / Jahdae Barron, Broncos Cobie Durant, Cowboys Kelee Ringo, Eagles Mike Sainristil, Commanders Roger McCreary / Ennis Rakestraw, Lions AJ Terrell, Falcons

title: Rams have not announced official QB2
summary: Sean McVay gave a recent press conference leading up to Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers where McVay addressed that both Stetson Bennett and Ty Simpson would backup Matthew Stafford. The twist is that McVay would not answer who the actual QB2 vs. the emergency QB3 would be. Bennett or Simpson? Both Bennett and […]
full_text: Sean McVay gave a recent press conference leading up to Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers where McVay addressed that both Stetson Bennett and Ty Simpson would backup Matthew Stafford . The twist is that McVay would not answer who the actual QB2 vs. the emergency QB3 would be. Bennett or Simpson? Both Bennett and Simpson are expected to be a massive drop off from Stafford, but one will be expected to handle the worst-case scenario over the other if Stafford goes down. You can watch the presser below, McVay says he is confident in both quarterbacks and that may be true. But which one is McVay more confident in filling in for Stafford? Regardless of that answer for Week 1, McVay said it was a fluid situation. For the last couple seasons the Rams had a clear back QB in Jimmy Garoppolo, and that is not the case going into 2026 as the Rams have no clear backup. It’s a situation to monitor and a developing story. Sean McVay explains why Stetson Bennett, Ty Simpson are 2A and 2B at QB (ramwire) “Sean McVay said on Friday that while Bennett is second on the depth chart , he views Stetson and Simpson as 2A and 2B behind Stafford. That obviously wasn’t the case with Jimmy Garoppolo and Bennett last season, but with two young quarterbacks on the roster, the Rams want to make sure both of them get reps during practice.“ LA Rams Going With ‘Different’ Plan Behind Matthew Stafford (heavy.com) “We look at it as two guys,” McVay told reporters on September 4. “I’ll tell you when I decide who’s going to be the actual 2 in the game. And I’ve talked to the players about it, but that’s something that they’re both going to continue to train, regardless of who ends up being up, and who’s the emergency third [QB]. I look at it as both of those guys are going to play. But you saw we listed Stetson as the 2, Ty as the 3, but I look at as the 2A/2B, and we’ll see how we approach the game.” McVay opened up about how it was “different than previous years.” Rams plan to bring entire team to season opener, including Donald (espn.com) “”Obviously one of the best things you can do is get out there and play football in 11-on-11 settings with pads, your eye progression, taking on some of the double-teams, different things like that,” McVay said. “So this week will be a big week for him in terms of how he feels. And then we’ll just kind of take it a day at a time and see where he’s at. “If he feels good enough to go, great. If not, I’ve got a lot of confidence in the other guys that’ll be ready to step up if that’s the case, that have really gotten all the reps anyways.” McVay also said Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua “is making good progress” as he rehabs a psoas (core/lower back) injury. Nacua first injured his psoas on Aug. 11 in a joint practice with the Dallas Cowboys . He returned to practice on Sunday.“ Rams Warned Against Costly Decision on Davante Adams (heavy.com) “Former sports agent Joel Corry, now an analyst for CBS Sports, wrote on September 4 that Adams has the 25th-highest cap hit in the NFL this coming season. He also noted, “Adams has the third-highest wide receiver figure at $28 million.” While Corry believes Adams is a “logical” candidate for a restructure, he argued against it.“ First Look: Rams take on 49ers in Australia to kick off 2026 season (therams) “Quarterback Brock Purdy played in nine games as he missed the middle of the season due to injury. He finished with 2,167 passing yards, 20 passing touchdowns and 10 interceptions as well as 147 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns. Backup quarterback Mac Jones had 2,151 passing yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions in 11 games. Both return for the 2026 season. Running back Christian McCaffrey played in all 17 games and had 1,202 rushing yards with 10 touchdowns and 924 receiving yards with seven touchdowns in his fourth season with the 49ers, returning for his fifth season this year.“ What is the Jaguars’ plan for Travis Hunter in Year 2? Plus, my ranking of the NFL’s top 5 cornerbacks (nfl.com) “It is uncommon for a slot defender to seamlessly transition to a CB1 role on the outside, but McDuffie excels wherever he’s asked to play. Earning a pair of All-Pro nods and winning two Super Bowls in his first four seasons, McDuffie has shown airtight coverage against slot receivers and outside pass catchers, while also displaying A+ instincts, awareness and diagnostic skills. As a “see ball, get ball” defender who can handle the stress of playing Cover 0 (no safety help, with an all-out blitz up front) in pivotal moments, McDuffie is built to play the CB1 role as an inside or outside cover man in a pass-happy league.“ Tutu Atwell ‘excited’ to be back with Rams after surprise trade from Dolphins (nfl.com) “When Atwell left for Miami, the intent seemed clear: It was time for Tutu to exit the shadows cast by the likes of Cooper Kupp , Puka Nacua , Davante Adams , etc., and create his own value. Instead, his value existed in familiarity. The Rams needed depth behind Nacua and Adams, while Atwell appeared to be available after failing to earn a top-three job in Miami’s receiving corps. A simple phone call fixed both situations. Now, Atwell is back in his NFL home and couldn’t be happier. “Nah, man, it don’t feel like I was gone,” Atwell said. “I’m back with my brothers, man. I just feel great and feel awesome just to be back here and with these great players and guys. I’m just excited.” Rams coaches have Les Snead to thank for making their lives a whole lot easier (ramblinfan) “The same team that got so much from one of the least expensive defenses in the NFL suddenly finds itself touted as one of the most talented units in NFL history. On paper, at least. Les Snead has built a Rams roster coaches will thank him for Spending copious amounts on new contracts with more than two dozen deals expiring next offseason seems crazy. And perhaps Snead is a bit eccentric. But his is also an inspired strategy if all the dominoes fall the right way.“ 13 Rams starters who will become free agents after 2026 season (ramswire) “That gives the Rams 13 key starters who could be playing their final season in horns. P Ethan Evans WR Puka Nacua WR Davante Adams DT Aaron Donald RG Kevin Dotson TE Colby Parkinson C Coleman Shelton LG Steve Avila OLB Byron Young DT Kobie Turner RT Warren McClendon Jr. LB Omar Speights (RFA) K Harrison Mevis (ERFA)“ Keeping Up With the 49ers: Week 1 in Melbourne, Australia (49ers.com) “ Day 1 wrapped up at the Melbourne Cricket Ground with AFL Finals action, giving the 49ers their first look at the venue they take over on gameday. With the first day in the books, the 49ers week in Melbourne is officially underway.“ Comment of the Day: “I don’t understand the super team, all in, etc. hype. For example, Lions have Jahmyr Gibbs 9, St. Brown 22, Aiden Hutchinson 30, Jared Goff 33, Penei Sewell 37, Jack Campbell 88. 6 players in the top 100, all paid top contracts at one point. Kerbie Joseph, Alim McNeil and Jamison Williams have also been paid. They are getting ready to pay Sam Laporta and Brian Branch big money. That will be 11 players paid top money or near for player contracts at some point. Lions are considered under achievers in my book but aren’t an all in or a super team per the media. What gives?? Why no label and super high expectations?“ -WeekLongDetention Fanpost of the Day:

title: Raiders’ Patrick Johnson a feel-good story, but veteran earned his spot
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are no strangers to preseason “phenoms”. Same can be said about the other 31 teams in the NFL, really. Usually, said standouts tend to be of the young variety, either an undrafted free agent (UDFA) or a player in their second or third year in the league. Case-in-point: Cian Slone. The […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - AUGUST 20: Defensive end Patrick Johnson #93 of the Las Vegas Raiders readies for play during the NFL preseason game between the Houston Texans and the Las Vegas Raiders on August 20, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are no strangers to preseason “phenoms”. Same can be said about the other 31 teams in the NFL, really. Usually, said standouts tend to be of the young variety, either an undrafted free agent (UDFA) or a player in their second or third year in the league. Case-in-point: Cian Slone. The undrafted rookie from North Carolina State shined in practices during training camp and produced in preseason action on both defense and special teams. But there was another edge rusher who did exactly that and more: Patrick Johnson. Like his 23-year-old counterpart Slone, Johnson stood out in practices and jumped out in preseason action on defense and special teams. So much so, the 28-year-old veteran heading into his sixth season in the NFL earned a 53-man roster spot while Slone was waived during cutdown day but returned to the practice squad. Johnson, who entered the league and spent the majority of is NFL career with the Philadelphia Eagles as a seventh-round pick (234th overall) in the 2021 NFL Draft, tops Slone in experience and and gameday production this preseason. And has the mentality required for NFL longshots as he was a July 27 signing by the Raiders — Slone in comparison was inked as an UDFA back on April 30. By The Numbers Patrick Johnson, Edge Rusher, 6th season 2025: 9 games (zero starts), 8 total tackles, 1 tackle for loss, 1 sack; 115 snaps on defense, 173 on special teams Career: 70 games (2 starts), 47 total tackles, 2 tackles for loss, 1 sack, 1 forced fumble, 1 fumble recovery; 523 snaps on defense, 1,328 snaps no special teams “You’ve got to believe in yourself before anyone else can believe in you,” Johnson told Raiders.com recently . “When it came to coming here, having my workout, I was so prepared. I told my wife, told my family, ‘Look, if they bring me in for a workout, I know I’m going to kill it. If they bring me in, I know I’m going to make this team.’” Johnson is a feel-good story, but he earned his roster spot — without question. The Tulane product finished preseason action with 13 total tackles, four tackles for loss, two sacks, and a forced fumble. That made the coaching staff and general manager John Spytek take notice. DE Patrick Johnson looks to solidify his roster spot on the Raiders this season, and feels he left everything out on the field tonight to earn that #Raiders pic.twitter.com/shu6rMxkIs — Raider Nation Radio (@RNR920AM) August 28, 2026 So much so for Spytek, he pinpointed Johnson as the player that changed his evaluation of him the most during camp. “I’ll give some respect and some props to Patrick Johnson,” Spytek said during his media availability this past Tuesday. “This is a guy that we signed on the eve of training camp, like, literally the eve of training camp, and credit to our pro department for setting up that workout and bringing quality guys in like him. And we had followed Patrick for many years with his career in Philadelphia and respected the kind of player and teammate and special teams player he is. “But every day he showed up and worked, and he got better and better. And you go to the last preseason game against the 49ers, and it’s a make-or-break game for a lot of guys and who makes the first tackle on the first kickoff is Patrick Johnson.” Spytek noted the preseason finale was indeed a make or break outing for roster hopefuls like Johnson and Slone, but it was the former that performed to make the 53-man roster. But the latter isn’t sliced liver as Slone made the practice squad and was someone that Spytek called out when asked about how the Achilles injury shelving third-round pick Keyron Crawford affected the edge rusher room. “Well, it certainly hurt, and we were counting on Key (Keyron Crawford), but it’s the game of football, and it’s the next man up mentality,” Spytek said. “So, we’re grateful to have Patrick Johnson in the room, somebody that’s played in this league and proven it, and have Cian on the practice squad too as a guy that we’re developing and see playing good football for us here coming up.” While not as locquacious as the general manager, head coach Klint Kubiak is in-sync with Spytek regarding Johnson. “Yeah, I would just echo all the things that Spy said yesterday, said Kubiak. “Since the moment he got here, all he’s done is produce, work hard and be a great teammate. Expect that to continue.” Two pleasant surprises for John Spytek and Brian Stark throughout training camp: Defensive linemen Patrick Johnson and Tonka Hemingway. #Raiders pic.twitter.com/XGG3usPyTR — Levi Edwards (@theleviedwards) September 1, 2026 With a core group of defensive ends/edge rushers featuring Maxx Crosby, Kwity Paye, and Malcolm Koonce, Johnson’s participation rate on defense isn’t projected to be overtly high. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard is likely to use a rotation as both games and seasons get deeper. Crosby will rarely leave the field (his uncanny stamina is simply ungodly) and both Paye and Koonce are going to get their fair share of defensive snaps. Johnson’s workload on Joe DeCamillis special teams units will likely be heavy, though. The 6-foot-2 and 248-pounder’s physicality, speed, and will were ever-present on special teams during the preseason and he has the experience and mentality to be a maven in DeCamillis’ group. Johnson joins a strong core of special teams mainstays in linebackers Tommy Eichenberg, Cody Lindenberg, and Segun Olubi, wide receiver Dareke Young, and cornerback Darrell Luter Jr. Olubi, who intially didn’t make the final 53 but was re-signed this past Monday after the Raiders placed second-year wide receiver Dont’e Thorton Jr. on injured reserve, noted a great special teams unit must showcase violence and attacking mindset. Johnson brings that in spades. “I’m a guy that can go out there and make plays,” Johnson said. “Be disruptive on defense, but also I can do it on special teams. I’m going to show my experience out there. I just want to show the coaches and the front office that y’all brought a dog in here. I’ve got a lot to prove left and we’re just getting started.”

title: Raiders Mailbag: What week will Fernando Mendoza make his 1st start, what will Raiders’ record be?
summary: The 53-man roster is set (for now), and we’re playing the waiting game for the Las Vegas Raiders’ season opener next Sunday against the Miami Dolphins. So, we’re previewing the 2026 campaign for this week’s mailbag. Let’s get to it! Q: What week will Fernando Mendoza make his first start, and what will the Raiders’ […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 27: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders looks to throw against the San Francisco 49ers in the second quarter of their preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The 49ers defeated the Raiders 18-12. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 53-man roster is set (for now), and we’re playing the waiting game for the Las Vegas Raiders’ season opener next Sunday against the Miami Dolphins. So, we’re previewing the 2026 campaign for this week’s mailbag. Let’s get to it! Q: What week will Fernando Mendoza make his first start, and what will the Raiders’ record be? A: I set the line at 6.5 games after Mendoza was drafted and before the schedule was released, and stuck to that for the majority of the summer. However, with the Los Angeles Rams, Myles Garrett and now Aaron Donald awaiting in Week 7, I’m wavering on that and it’s time to adjust the line. Putting a rookie quarterback in front of that defensive line for his first start is a very bad idea. Like very bad, LOL! So, I think a more realistic expectation would be Week 8 against the Jets. Maybe Klint Kubiak pushes it to Week 9 against the 49ers to avoid Mendoza’s first start having all of the baggage that comes with an East Coast trip. But both of those games are on the road anyway, and the midway point of the season seems like a good place for a rookie to have some time to adjust to the NFL and still get enough reps to build on moving into 2027 and beyond. Record-wise, I see the Raiders being 2-5 with home wins against the Dolphins and Chiefs and losses to the Chargers, Saints, Patriots, Bills and Rams heading into the Jets matchup. That brings up another point (and I imagine this is what you’re getting at with the question) where if Las Vegas isn’t winning with Kirk Cousins at quarterback , it’s going to be hard to justify not making the change. I’m all for being patient with Mendoza and not throwing him into the fire before he’s ready, but at some point, Kubiak has to see what the kid has and how he handles adversity. Plus, as a head coach, you’re going to lose the locker room if the team isn’t winning and you’re not making a quarterback change, especially if Mendoza is showing out in practice. I know I’ve said this before, but I’m going to keep pounding this drum that the Raiders should follow the Patriots’ model with Drake Maye. In 2024, New England won its season opener and then dropped to 1-4 while it was clear Jacoby Brissett wasn’t getting the job done, paving the way for Maye to make his first start in Week 6. Q: I keep having this argument. The Raiders are not going to make the NFL number one pick an Emergency QB. The optics are horrible if they do this. What is take your this? A: This might come off as me being an egomanic, but I think I’m at least a part of the reason for this line of thinking. In a mailbag column at the beginning of August, someone asked me about the backup quarterback plan, and I threw out the idea of having Aidan O’Connell as the QB2 while Mendoza is the emergency QB. My full answer can be found via this link , and below is the gist of my logic. If the reason for sitting Mendoza is so that he doesn’t get thrown into the fire before he’s ready and ruin his confidence, then it would make more sense for AOC to be the backup because he’d be the one to go in the game if Cousins gets injured rather than the rookie getting thrown into a chaotic situation. But if it’s the other way around, then Mendoza’s first regular-season appearance is coming off the bench cold and having to play in a game that he didn’t get to prepare for as the starter. To be clear, I’m not saying this is going to happen or even what should happen. It’s just an option out there that makes sense (to me, at least) and could be part of the reason why O’Connell is on the roster. You’re absolutely right that it’s a bad look if the No. 1 pick of the draft is third on the depth chart to begin his career, and I’m sure the big media outlets will run with that and call the Raiders stupid. Dan Orlovsky will probably be taking victory laps and be so excited that he celebrates with an unflavored, unseasoned chicken dinner! My counter to that: Who the hell cares? Kubiak and the rest of the organization need to be focused on the big picture, and if they think that having Mendoza be the emergency quarterback is best for his development, do it! The Raiders and Kubiak have to stay true to themselves and do what they think is best for the long-term plan. That’s what this season is all about. Let people have their fun and get their laughs in now. Because if Mendoza ends up being a stud after beginning his career as the QB3, it’ll be our turn to do the laughing. I feel like this is my Dan Hurley moment, LOL! Q: Is either Kirk Cousins, Aidan O’Connell or Maxx Crosby traded before the Nov. 8 trade deadline? A: On the topic, I don’t think Cousins has much (if any) trade value at this stage in his career. Especially if he isn’t starting anymore, that likely means he wasn’t playing well in the first half of the season. Maybe an injury changes the situation, but we’ve already seen that the league doesn’t view the 38-year-old as a starting-caliber quarterback anymore due to the lack of interest in him during free agency. Plus, even if Cousins isn’t playing, he brings more value as Mendoza’s mentor than a sixth- or seventh-round pick would, in my opinion. O’Connell, on the other hand, is younger and has starting experience to be more tradable (I think that’s a word) if a team has a quarterback injury. On top of that, he becomes expendable if Mendoza is starting or is even the backup. There’s a lot of moving parts in the situation, so predicting if AOC does get traded would just be a pure guess from me, to be honest. But I definitely think that’s on the table. Now for the big one: Maxx Crosby. My answer is tied to the previous question about the record. If the Raiders aren’t hitting the ground running, contending teams are going to be calling about Crosby heading into the trade deadline, especially if he’s playing well and there are no injury concerns about his knee. Whether or not another club is willing to meet the two first-round picks price tag remains to be seen, but I think Kubiak and John Spytek will have to be honest with themselves about the direction of the team. Crosby is the best player on the roster, but he’s also a 29-year-old on a team that’s likely two years away from being a legitimate contender. If the Raiders are, say, 2-6 heading into the Week 9 trade deadline, the “two years away” statement is reinforced, and getting something like first- and second-round picks is the smarter long-term move than keeping a player who is probably nearing the end of his prime given his age. I love Maxx. He’s my favorite player on the team and is probably on the Mt. Rushmore of Raiders during my lifetime (I was born in ‘93, for the record). But when I look at the long-term vision of the team, I think getting a couple of young and talented players with a pair of high draft picks is more valuable. Plus, that would allow Crosby to go chase a ring if it isn’t going to happen in Vegas. All of that is a long-winded way of saying: yes, I can definitely see Maxx Crosby getting traded at the deadline. Q: Why is Dylan Laube on the roster? What exactly has he done from the time he was drafted that compels this team to keep him yet again? Why not go with someone/anyone else that could surprise and have actual upside? A: The Raiders started training camp with rookie Mike Washington Jr., Laube, Chris Collier and rookie UDFA Roman Hemby behind Ashton Jeanty, and Dare Ogunbowale didn’t even get a carry in the first preseason game because he was signed so late. In other words, there wasn’t much competition for the third running back spot. Also, I thought Laube played pretty well in the preseason. He really stood out to me in the Texans game with five carries for 27…

title: Raiders News: Maxx Crosby trade deadline chatter already starting
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders put what looks like the finishing touches on their initial 53-man roster this week, and the 2026 season hasn’t even started yet. However, Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox is already discussing a potential roster shake-up that a lot of Raider Nation wouldn’t be happy about: trading defensive end Maxx Crosby. In a […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NV - NOVEMBER 17: Maxx Crosby #98 of the Las Vegas Raiders looks on from the field during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at Allegiant Stadium on November 17, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders put what looks like the finishing touches on their initial 53-man roster this week, and the 2026 season hasn’t even started yet. However, Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox is already discussing a potential roster shake-up that a lot of Raider Nation wouldn’t be happy about: trading defensive end Maxx Crosby. In a column titled “Bold Trade Predictions Before the 2026 NFL Season Kicks Off”, Knox predicted the Dallas Cowboys will trade 2027 and 2028 first-round picks and edge defender Rashan Gary for Crosby, citing Cowboys owner Jerry Jones’ July remarks that Dallas never closed the door on acquiring the five-time Pro Bowler as justification. On why Las Vegas would accept: “The Raiders seem content to keep Crosby after their offseason trade with the Baltimore Ravens fell through. However, they could revisit the idea of flipping the 29-year-old if they’re struggling to compete in late October,” Knox wrote. “After taking Fernando Mendoza No. 1 overall, Las Vegas won’t be in the market for a quarterback in next year’s draft. However, it will be looking for long-term pieces to put around Mendoza. Trading Crosby, who could be past his prime by the time the Raiders are ready to contend, could get Las Vegas a very strong return.” While this wouldn’t be popular within the fanbase, that’d be a really hard deal for John Sptyek to pass up. Gary fills the immediate need at edge, while the pair of first-rounders help build for the future. However, this deal seems very unrealistic. It was reported that the Cowboys’ team doctor, Dr. Daniel Cooper, was part of the Ravens’ review team for Crosby’s knee this spring. That makes it pretty hard to see Dallas not just matching but beating Baltimore’s deal if its team doctor potentially has concerns over the player’s long-term health. Also, the Cowboys just traded for Gary in the offseason and drafted edge Malachi Lawrence in the first round, on top of having 2025 second-round pick Donovan Ezeiruaku at the position. But if a deal like this is on the table by Nov. 10, Spytek would have something to think about. In Other Raiders’ Links: NFL Draft prospects to watch: With College Football getting going this weekend, find six wide receivers and five defensive tackle prospects to keep tabs on for the draft. Game-by-game prediction: S&BP’s Ray Aspuria takes a stab at predicting the Raiders’ record for the 2026 season. When should Fernando Mendoza start?: The Princess of Darkness and current CBS Sports Analyst, Amy Trask, answers the question on all of Raider Nation’s mind , stating: “It needs to be a collaborative decision” between Klint Kubiak, John Sptyek and the rest of the scouting staff. The case for starting Mendoza: “The Raiders starting Kirk Cousins makes sense. But short of a miracle, Fernando Mendoza has to play,” the California Post’s Vincent Bonsignore posted on X/Twitter promoting his column . “A lot [of] respect to Brady & Mahomes, but they had their journeys. Mendoza has his. He was drafted No. 1 to play, not follow someone else’s timeline.” Join the conversation! title: Dolphins draft prospects 2027: Five players to watch in Texas State vs. Texas
summary: The NFL season is still a few days away, but the college schedule is well underway with Week 1 games already having started. This year, I wanted to bring a new piece to The Phinsider taking a look at college prospects from a college game on the schedule. The goal is share some of the […]
full_text: ORLANDO, FL - DECEMBER 31: Arch Manning #16 of the Texas Longhorns runs with the ball during the Cheez-It Citrus Bowl game between the Michigan Wolverines and the Texas Longhorns on December 31, 2025 at Campting World Stadium in Orlando, Fl. (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The NFL season is still a few days away, but the college schedule is well underway with Week 1 games already having started. This year, I wanted to bring a new piece to The Phinsider taking a look at college prospects from a college game on the schedule. The goal is share some of the 2027 NFL Draft prospects who could land on the Miami Dolphins’ radar when the 2026 season ends and we start to move toward the draft. This week, we’ll look at the Texas State vs. Texas game. Kickoff is Saturday, September 5, 2026, at 3:30 p.m. Eastern, with ESPN on the broadcast. The game will be at Darrell K Royal—Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, Texas on the University of Texas campus. Below are five players to watch from the game. These are not necessarily the top-ranked prospects for each team, but they are players who could be factors when the NFL Draft rolls around. Texas 2027 Draft prospects Arch Manning, quarterback (Redshirt Junior) – Manning is in contention to be the first-overall pick in 2027, assuming his play lives up to the offseason hype. Manning still has eligibility left, so he could also elect to return to college for another year. He has the potential to be something special; he has the tools and the arm to succeed in the NFL, and he has the pedigree. He has to be consistent and he needs to turn Texas into a contender this year if he wants to hold on to that top spot like uncles Payton and Eli. Collin Simmons, edge (Junior) – Simmons could prove to be the first edge rusher to come off the board in the spring. He is nasty, especially when he comes in with a speed rush, using his bend to get around the corner. He knows how to set the corner and attack running backs as well, though he will miss tackles. If a team that already has a quarterback in place lands the first-overall pick, Simmons could prove to be the pick. Derek Williams, Jr., safety (Redshirt Junior) – Williams came into Texas as one of the top high school prospects out of Louisiana. Nothing has gone the way anyone expected. A 2024 injury ended that season early and, when he returned to the field in 2025, he settled into a depth role. He is expected to start at free safety this year and he has the size and speed an NFL team could look for at safety, but there is going to be some gamble that he can put the knee injury behind him and reach the potential he had coming out of high school. This season will be critical for Williams if he plans on declaring for the draft. Texas State 2027 Draft prospects Jaylen Early, guard (Redshirt Senior) – Early began his college career at Florida State, then transferred to Missouri, and is now at Texas State. He has primarily served as a backup guard but should be the starter all year at Texas State. The experience will be important in his development. He does have experience playing at tackle, but is probably better suited at guard. He could use the exposure of a game against a big-name opponent like Texas to show off his potential for the NFL. He is probably destined for a later-round pick or undrafted free agent signing, but a strong performance on Saturday and throughout the year could push him a little earlier. Beau Sparks, wide receiver (Junior) – A slot receiver with glue for hands, Sparks saw a massive production jump from 2024 (25 receptions, 271 yards, 2 touchdowns) to 2025 (84 receptions, 1200 yards, 10 touchdowns) and likely continues that upward trajectory into this season. He is a precise route runner, and he has the speed to create separation against man, but he excels in finding the soft spots in the zone. He is probably a day three prospect, but one who could find a solid role in the NFL if he declares.

title: Patriots 2026 scouting report for S Jaylen Reed
summary: After months of speculation, the New England Patriots finally pulled the trigger in late August and traded Kayshon Boutte. The fourth-year wide receiver was sent to the Houston Texans in a package deal that included a 2028 seventh-round draft choice as well as a player the organization has apparently coveted since he entered the league […]
full_text: Foxborough, MA - August 25: New England Patriots safety Jaylen Reed warms up at practice at Gillette Stadium on August 25, 2026. (Photo by Danielle Parhizkaran/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images After months of speculation, the New England Patriots finally pulled the trigger in late August and traded Kayshon Boutte. The fourth-year wide receiver was sent to the Houston Texans in a package deal that included a 2028 seventh-round draft choice as well as a player the organization has apparently coveted since he entered the league as a sixth-round draft selection the previous year. And so, Jaylen Reed now finds himself a member of the Patriots. Hard facts Name: Jaylen Reed Position: Safety Jersey number: 23 Opening day age: 23 (1/29/2003) Measurements : 5’11 5/8”, 212 lbs, 30 3/8” arm length, 9” hand size, 4.49s 40-yard dash, 33 1/2” vertical jump, 19 bench press reps, 9.26 Relative Athletic Score Experience NFL: Houston Texans (2025), New England Patriots (2026-) | College: Penn State (2021-24) A two-sport athlete growing up, who excelled on the gridiron and the track, Reed was rated a four-star recruit heading toward college. As such, he generated considerable buzz from his sophomore campaign at Martin Luther King Jr. High School in Detroit on. Among the schools to offer him were powerhouses such as Georgia, Nebraska, Oregon and USC. Ultimately, however, he decided to take his talents to Happy Valley. In four seasons at Penn State, Reed started 29 of 50 games — all of those coming over his final two seasons — and was twice voted to an All-Big Ten team (second team 2024, honorable mention 2023). He still had to remain on the board until the sixth round of the 2025 NFL Draft, before the Texans decided to bring him in. In his lone seasons in Houston, he played in nine games with three starts and registered one takeaway. Scouting report Strengths: Reed plays with his hair on fire, and excels especially when being allowed to use his aggressiveness as a downhill defender. In run support, he attacks with a purpose and quickly shoots down from the second or third levels to get to the ball carrier; he has a fast trigger and the proper acceleration to get involved, as well as the physicality and power to get runners to the ground even when meeting them head-on. Against the pass, Reed works best with the play in front of him, either in zone coverage or when employed as a blitzer. He is a positionally flexible player capable of lining up in various spots on defense and special teams. Weaknesses: Reed’s play style is one of his defining features, but it also can work against him. He has a tendency to be too aggressive with his reads and angles, which in turn prompts him to fall for misdirection or lose track of his assignments in man-to-man coverage. His tackling technique can also suffer from him coming in too hot, resulting in some bad misses. In general, he has solid speed but does not provide high-end range as the last line of defense. He furthermore struggled with injuries in 2025, even though durability was no particular concern back in college. 2025 review Stats : 9 games (3 starts) | 173 defensive snaps (14.9%), 113 special teams snap (21.7%) | 18 tackles, 4 missed tackles (18.2%), 1 FR | 12 targets, 12 catches surrendered (100%), 143 yards, 1 TD | 1 special teams tackle, 1 missed tackle (50.0%) | 0 penalties Season recap: Coming off his final year at Penn State, Reed was invited to both the Senior Bowl and the Scouting Combine. He declined the first invitation and did not do a full program of drills in Indianapolis, and eventually fell to the 187th slot in the draft (roughly one full round lower than his projection on the Arif Hasan consensus big board ). Reed consequently had to start his career fighting for a roster spot, but that battle never truly began: in early August, he sprained his knee in practice and had to sit out the remainder of training camp plus his rookie preseason. When roster cuts came, he was placed on injured reserve with the intention of eventually being activated again. That is precisely what happened ahead of Houston’s Week 7 game in Seattle. Reed made his NFL debut that Sunday, playing 19 snaps on special teams and none on defense — a theme for his early 2025 campaign. Exactly one month after his comeback, and after having played just one defensive snap in his first four games, however, he had a breakout performance. Going up against one of the best teams in the NFL, the Buffalo Bills, the rookie registered 12 tackles as well as a fumble recovery. It's a catch and FUMBLE! The @HoustonTexans defense comes up big once again. BUFvsHOU on Prime Video Also streaming on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/35yBvin0oP — NFL (@NFL) November 21, 2025 The Bills game gave the Texans’ coaches confidence in Reed, but his momentum was disrupted by another injury the following week. He reportedly broke a metal plate in his forearm, a remnant from an old college injury, and was again sent to injured reserve. And, once again, he was declared as a return player — a plan that did not materialize until after the regular season. Reed did, however, start both of the Texans’s playoff games and was on the field for 82% of their defensive snaps in the tournament. He registered five combined tackles without any true impact plays in Houston’s win over the Steelers and season-ending loss to the Patriots. 2026 preview Position: Fox safety | Ability: Depth player/Role player | Contract: Signed through 2028 (2029 UFA) What will be his role? With the Patriots set atop their safety depth chart, Reed projects as a rotational third and fourth option at the position as well as a possible multi-purpose special teamer. As for his actual role, his history suggests he will be used mostly as a so-called star: a box safety/linebacker hybrid capable of patrolling the second level both versus the pass and the run. What is his growth potential? Entering only his second season in the NFL, Reed’s journey is obviously just getting started. There have been some promising moments back in 2025 already, and he very well should be capable of building on those. If he does, he might become a regular third safety early in his Patriots tenure with the potential to earn a starting role as soon as 2027. Does he have positional versatility? Reed is a positionally-flexible player capable of lining up both in the box, deep and in the slot on defense. In the kicking game, he has experience on five units: kickoff return and coverage, punt return and coverage, and field goal/extra point block. What is his salary cap situation? When the Patriots acquired Reed via trade, they took on his rookie contract sans the signing bonus proration that remained in Houston. This means that there are no guarantees left in the pact, and that it only consists of salary payments from now though 2028. This year’s portion of the pact is worth $1.005 million. How safe is his roster spot? Barring injury, Reed should remain on New England’s roster throughout the season. Not only does he have upside as a developmental safety, he also can contribute right away in the kicking game. That being said, the financial investment in him is relatively minimal and nothing the team would be afraid from moving on from if his performances don’t look the part. That scenario seems unlikely, though. Summary: Fairly or not, Reed will be in the spotlight all season: that is the burden of somebody involved in a player-for-player trade. The Patriots, of course, will not entertain any comparisons between him and Kayshon Boutte; their focus is on getting him ready to contribute and possibly develop into a starter-level player come the 2027 season — one where he very well could find himself as the No. 2 next to Craig Woodson. What do you think about Jaylen Reed heading into the 2026 season? Will he or Kayshon Boutte play a more prominent role for their new teams? And is he a long-term solution at safety? Please head down…

summary: The last time Drake Maye played an NFL game, his top three wide receivers were Kayshon Boutte, Mack Hollins and Stefon Diggs. While Hollins remains with the Patriots from their loss to the Seattle Seahawks in February’s Super Bowl, the other two have since left New England. In their place, offseason acquisitions A.J. Brown and […]
full_text: Foxborough, MA - June 11: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and wide receiver A.J. Brown at minicamp on June 11, 2026. (Photo by Barry Chin/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images The last time Drake Maye played an NFL game, his top three wide receivers were Kayshon Boutte, Mack Hollins and Stefon Diggs. While Hollins remains with the Patriots from their loss to the Seattle Seahawks in February’s Super Bowl, the other two have since left New England. In their place, offseason acquisitions A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs will fill starting roles this fall. And while both Boutte and Diggs were productive working with Maye, the likes of Brown and Doubs are, on paper, an upgrade. Unsurprisingly, there is quite a bit of excitement heading into Wednesday’s season opener against those very same Seahawks — starting with the Patriots’ quarterback himself. “It’s hard not to be excited,” Maye told reporters at Gillette Stadium on Saturday. “You love guys in that room, in our skill position room, that we have that make my job easier and that make me look good. “And that’s with our skill group last year. I was looking forward to seeing what this skill group does because I think another year for the guys that were here in this system to grow and be even better, and the new guys that come in that have been players in this league — look forward to getting the ball as fast as I can, as much as I can. Those guys can make plays. I got the best seat in the house when I throw it to them or watch them run.” Brown and Doubs project as the main targets in a wide receiver group that also consists of 2025 holdovers Hollins, DeMario Douglas — the projected starter in the slot — and sophomores Kyle Williams and Efton Chism. In addition, the Patriots also invested a third-round draft selection in Eli Raridon to complement starting tight end Hunter Henry; they furthermore get running back duo Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson back. Together, all of them give Maye a supporting cast that might be one of the most talented in recent Patriots history. It certainly beats what the young passer had at his disposal in his first two seasons in the league. The 24-year-old got a taste of that already in training camp. “It’s a huge confidence booster for me of seeing them time and time again go up and make plays,” he said. “And fortunately enough, growing up, my dad played quarterback, and he always said, ‘It’s hard to force it to one guy.’ Knowing that those guys will make plays when you feel like the game’s moving and you feel like the offense is in a groove, that just comes naturally. That’s what you have seen with guys that have big games, and you can see from last year of different guys having big games. That’s one of the best things about my position is just seeing everybody do their part and do their job well and how rewarding that is.”

title: Patriots 2026 scouting report for OL Greg Van Roten
summary: The New England Patriots offensive line depth suffered a blow in the first game of the summer. The preseason opener against the Indianapolis Colts saw the team’s fourth and fifth interior linemen, Ben Brown and Andrew Rupcich, both go down with injuries. In order to not become vulnerable up front, the Patriots explored the free […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Greg van Roten #70 of the New England Patriots looks on after the preseason game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots offensive line depth suffered a blow in the first game of the summer. The preseason opener against the Indianapolis Colts saw the team’s fourth and fifth interior linemen, Ben Brown and Andrew Rupcich, both go down with injuries. In order to not become vulnerable up front, the Patriots explored the free agency market. They ended up bringing in a player with immense experience and the necessary versatility to serve as a super-sub along the interior O-line. Hard facts Name: Greg Van Roten Position: Guard/Center Jersey number: 70 Opening day age: 36 (2/26/1990) Measurements : 6’3”, 305 lbs, 9 1/” hand size, 32 1/2” arm length, 5.12s 40-yard dash, 7.98s 3-cone drill, 4.60s short shuttle, 34 1/2” vertical jump, 9’4” broad jump, 31 bench press reps, 9.31 Relative Athletic Score Experience NFL: Green Bay Packers (2012-13), Seattle Seahawks (2014), Jacksonville Jaguars (2017), Carolina Panthers (2017-19), New York Jets (2020-21), Buffalo Bills (2022), Las Vegas Raiders (2023), New York Giants (2024-25), New England Patriots (2026-) | College: Penn (2008-11) An all-state offensive tackle at at Chaminade High School in Mineola, NY, Van Roten spent his college career at Penn and started all 30 games he appeared in. The two-time first-team All-Ivy League selection (2010, 2011) subsequently joined the Packers as an undrafted free agent — the beginning of a journey that took him to nine different NFL teams so far as well as one in the CFL. Van Roten’s career started quietly. Despite entering the pros in 2012, his first consistent action came after he moved north of the border for a two-year stint with the Toronto Argonauts (2015-16). His first start in the NFL, meanwhile, did not come until 2018. From that point on, however, he managed to get semi-regular opportunities:with the exception of a two-year period in 2021 and 2022, he started all 91 of his games — including 51 straight over the last three seasons. In total, Van Roten has played 148 NFL games with 105 starts. He also appeared in 35 games in the CFL to bring his career total to 183 contests against professional competition. Scouting report Strengths: At 6-foot-3, 305 pounds, Van Roten has adequate size to compete along the interior offensive line. He also has a solid athletic foundation, even though the 9.31 Relative Athletic Score he posted in 2012 may no longer be entirely relevant 14 years later. What is relevant is his pass protection. He plays with good patience, uses his hands well, has an advanced understanding of attack angles, and shows some nimble feet to not leave himself exposed. Add his aforementioned experience as well as impressive recent durability, and you get a player capable of entering the lineup and performing at a solid level whenever asked to. Weaknesses: Having turned 36 in February, Van Roten is the oldest player on the Patriots’ current roster. While still capable of handling a heavy workload as evidenced by his 2025 campaign in New York, there are questions about his trajectory from a physical perspective. His run blocking is an example of that. He doesn’t display the same core strength he showed earlier in his career, and doesn’t have the burst out of his stance and reach as a zone-blocker his pre-draft testing would suggest he should have. Adding to this is a relative lack of length as well as the occasional lapse picking up stunts or line games. 2025 review Stats : 17 games (17 starts) | 1,150 offensive snaps (100%), 44 special teams snaps (9.9%) | 26 QB pressures surrendered (3 sacks, 1 hit, 22 hurries) | 2 penalties (incl. 0 declined/offsetting) Season recap: Van Roten’s first season with the Giants was a success, prompting the organization to re-sign him to another one-year contract in March. The $3.25 million deal set the stage for him to resume his role as the team’s starting right guard, and there never was any doubt about his status even as New York stumbled its way to a 4-13 campaign that saw the firing of head coach Brian Daboll in November. While the club as a whole was in turmoil, Van Roten proved himself a steady and generally reliable presence. Even at age 35, he managed to start all 17 games and play 100% of the Giants’ offensive snaps for a second straight year — bringing his snap total to 2,275 between his 2024 and 2025 campaigns. Along the way, he performed at a solid level particularly as a pass protector. After giving up 35 quarterback pressures including seven sacks the previous year, he reduced those numbers to 26 and three, respectively. He never surrendered more than three disruptions in a game in 2025, and was credited with a clean slate in four out of his five final games to close out the season. Despite his success, however, re-signing Van Roten was not made a priority by the Giants’ new brass heading into 2026. 2026 preview Position: Right guard/Left guard/Center | Ability: Fringe starter/Role player | Contract: Signed through 2026 (2027 UFA) What will be his role? Even though he is coming off one of the best seasons of his NFL career, Van Roten will not be a starter for the Patriots in 2026. Instead, he and Ben Brown will serve as a top backups behind the interior line trio of Alijah Vera-Tucker, Jared Wilson and Mike Onwenu. With Brown nursing an injury suffered in preseason, Van Roten projects as the super sub up front to start the year; once his teammate returns, the two are likely to split responsibilities: Van Roten will be the top backup guard, with Brown the No. 2 center. What is his growth potential? Given his age, Van Roten effectively holding his level would be a success this season. Time will tell whether or not he is capable of doing so. At the end of the day, conventional wisdom suggests that he is on a downward trajectory — something reflected by the fact that he remained unsigned as a free agent until August. Does he have positional versatility? Van Roten has precisely the versatility the Patriots are looking for. While mostly a right guard in his career — 69.5% of his snaps have come at this position — he also has started games at left guard and center. In addition, he has been a regular on field goal and extra point protection throughout his career. What is his salary cap situation? The Patriots signed Van Roten to a one-year, $3 million contact but he actually is carrying a $4.5 million cap number into 2026. Why? Because he has $1.5 million in playing time incentives in his pact classified as likely to be earned (which, if fully or partially unearned, would give New England cap credit in 2027). As for the base structure of the deal, it consists of a $1.48 million salary, $500,000 signing bonus proration, and $1.02 million in active roster bonuses. A combined $1 million — $500,000 each through his salary and signing bonus — is fully guaranteed. How safe is his roster spot? Despite joining the Patriots late, Van Roten was a lock to make the roster from the moment he signed his contract. Given its structure and the fact that the Patriots’ interior offensive line depth is a question mark outside of him, particularly to start the year, there is no question that he will remain on the team through 2026. Summary: Van Roten is an interesting player due to his experience and the fact that he played some of the best football of his career just last season. Ideally, the Patriots won’t given him any meaningful snaps on offense this year, but if they have to they certainly could be in worse shape. What do you think about Greg Van Roten heading into the 2026 season? Will he see any playing time? Will it be him or Ben Brown as the first man up along the interior offensive line? Please head down to the comment section to…

title: Christian Gonzalez remains focused on today amid contract negotiations
summary: The New England Patriots are just four days away from their regular-season opener against the Seattle Seahawks, and star cornerback Christian Gonzalez remains without a contract extension. So, will Gonzalez play Wednesday night? “I’m focused on today, right now, this practice,” Gonzalez said. Gonzalez, who has not committed to playing throughout the week, reiterated those […]
full_text: Jul 28, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez (0) speaks to the media after practice at training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New England Patriots are just four days away from their regular-season opener against the Seattle Seahawks, and star cornerback Christian Gonzalez remains without a contract extension. So, will Gonzalez play Wednesday night? “I’m focused on today, right now, this practice,” Gonzalez said. Gonzalez, who has not committed to playing throughout the week, reiterated those comments during his Saturday media availability when he asked about his ongoing contract situation. Earlier this week, Mike Vrabel noted the team will need to prepare for any players’ availability across the roster. “We have to prepare for everything to potentially happen, whether that is players’ availability through multiple different reasons,” Vrabel said. “So, we will have to be ready for a lot of things, and as we work here into Week 1 and the craziness of the National Football League and the journey that we are about to go on.” On Saturday, Gonzalez was again present for the start of practice, but said he did not know whether momentum was being made toward a deal. The 24-year old has recently admitted his frustration that no deal has been reached. As for head coach Mike Vrabel, he wouldn’t describe it that way. “I wouldn’t use the word frustrating,” Vrabel said. “I appreciate how our players feel and their emotions. I think that’s part of life. But, I can’t let that be frustrating. I want to be able to coach him, and help him improve as a player and a person, and help our football team and help our coaches.” As a former player turned head coach, Vrabel finds himself in an interesting spot when it comes to these negotiations. “I think it’s an interesting dynamic,” he said. “I’ve been on both sides. I think what’s important for me is to try to communicate, try to explain the players that we really want to build around and have. I’ve done that with Gonzo, and everybody knows that. “I don’t get involved in the negotiations, per se. But I certainly want to be involved in trying to get the situation resolved. That’s really what I try to do throughout my job, my day here. What the issues are, or what’s in front of us, and what we have to do to help the team. But, it’s a delicate balance we have to wage.”
