title: NY Giants aim for good start after John Harbaugh’s rigorous summer
summary: The New York Giants’ season-opening game against the Dallas Cowboys next Sunday night might not be a “must-win” game for the Giants. It sure would, though, be a significant one. The Giants have begun seasons 0-2 or worse in 10 of the last 13 years. It seems appropriate that the Giants will begin the John […]
full_text: John Harbaugh | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants’ season-opening game against the Dallas Cowboys next Sunday night might not be a “must-win” game for the Giants. It sure would, though, be a significant one. The Giants have begun seasons 0-2 or worse in 10 of the last 13 years. Season starts since 2013 Tom Coughlin 2013 — 0-6 (7-9 finish) 2014 — 0-2 (6-10 finish) 2015 — 0-2 (6-10 finish) Ben McAdoo 2016 — 2-0 (that extended to 10-4, then an 11-5 finish and a playoff berth) 2017 — 0-5 | 1-8 (3-13 finish | McAdoo, GM Jerry Reese fired with four games remaining and the Giants 2-10) Pat Shurmur 2018 — 1-7 (5-11 finish) 2019 — 0-2 | 2-11 (4-12 finish) Joe Judge 2020 — 0-5 | 1-7 (6-10 finish) 2021 — 1-5 (4-13 finish) Brian Daboll 2022 — 6-1 (9-7-1 finish … wild-card round victory over Minnesota Vikings) 2023 — 1-5 (6-11 finish) 2024 — 1-3 | 2-13 (3-14 finish) 2025 — 0-3 | Daboll fired at 2-8 (4-13 finish) It seems appropriate that the Giants will begin the John Harbaugh era in a nationally-televised game against the Cowboys. The Giants and Cowboys have played seven times in season-opening games since 2012. The Giants are 1-6 in those games, with their only victory coming in 2016. The memory of the 40-0 whitewashing by Dallas in 2023, the last time the teams met in a season-opener, is still fresh for Giants fans. The Giants hired Harbaugh, with 15 winning seasons, 12 playoff appearances, and a Super Bowl title in 18 years with the Baltimore Ravens, in an effort to get an organization that has lost its way since the 2011 Super Bowl victory, back on track. One of the things Harbaugh has to fix is the Giants’ history of burying themselves by the middle of October. Sometimes, by the end of September. The Ravens started the 2025 season 1-5, so Harbaugh is not immune to poor starts. Still, his track record is the antithesis of how the Giants have started seasons. Harbaugh’s Ravens went 12-6 in 18 season-opening games. In home openers under Harbaugh, the Ravens were 15-3. Part of that early-season success has to be that Harbaugh pushes players harder in the spring and summer than most current coaches. Harbaugh uses padded practices as much as the Collective Bargaining Agreement will allow, and generally keeps players on the field as long as the rules say he can. Even jog-throughs in West Virginia lasted 2½ hours. Harbaugh’s methods don’t need validation. His resume speaks for itself. The Giants, though, are long overdue for a change in their fortunes. Veteran cornerback Greg Newsome, who competed against Harbaugh’s team while with the Cleveland Browns, said the coach runs “tough, gritty” practices. “We’re going to work, and I like that,” Newsome said during training camp. “There’s no off days for us in terms of not competing. He’s going to make sure we compete.” Veteran defensive tackle D.J. Reader also lauded Harbaugh’s focus on getting the most out of each day during training camp. “You’ve got to callous the body,” Reader said. “The thing that’s important in football is callousing the body to be ready to take on those blows throughout the season, because you’re going to get chinks in your armor, and if you didn’t build your armor up enough to be able to withstand those hits, those dents, those little scratches you’ll take in your armor, then shame on you. “I think it’s important to be able to callous the body. Do it with intent. Be smart about it, but you have to callous the body to go out there and play this game. You’re not just going to roll out there, roll out of bed, and be able to go out there on Sundays and get it done.” Several times in recent years the Giants have employed the “go easy in the summer, then roll out of bed in Week 1 and go play” approach. The results have been mostly ugly. If things don’t go well at the beginning of this season, they certainly will not have that as an excuse. Tight end Isaiah Likely spent four years in Baltimore before following Harbaugh to New York. “That first two weeks we had in Greenbrier, out of 11 days, 10 practices, I feel like that’s normal to me. Like, I’m just – if I wake up, I’m putting on cleats. That’s just the mantra I have,” Likely said. “So, hearing how Giants training camp was in the past, that was kind of mind-boggling to me, but I feel like the guys embraced it. We had a good time in Greenbrier, and then when we got here, I feel like now everybody’s on the same mantra as, if we’re in the building, it’s all ball.” The Giants are 2.5-point underdogs against the Cowboys, per FanDuel Sportsbook . It is, of course, a Sunday night game. It is at home. It is Harbaugh’s first game. It is a division game, in a division where the Giants have been the poor, down-trodden step-child for a long while now. It is the first chance for the Giants to show the NFL that they are not the same old Giants. Oh, and in Week 2 the Giants have to travel across the country to face the Los Angeles Rams. The team that is favored to win the 2027 Super Bowl. The team some are already saying has a legitimate chance to go 17-0 this season. The team with Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald, Matthew Stafford, and a host of other star players. So, yeah, winning against the Cowboys on opening night takes on added importance. If the Giants are going to avoid what has become their annual 0-2 start, they would seem to have a better chance to do that in Week 1 than Week 2. Brandon Lee Gowton of the newly-relaunched NFC East Mixtape podcast and Bleeding Green Nation recognized the importance of the beginning of the season for the Giants when he said this: “It’s super-important for the Giants to get off to a great start this season … If you beat the Cowboys, which they have struggled to do so often now, especially in games that truly mattered, that would truly set the tone tone that you bring in John Harbaugh, this is a new era. We have Jaxson Dart here. “I think the Giants really need to win that first game, or at least split with the Rams in that Week 2 game, because once you do that the schedule opens up a bit and I think they can rattle off some wins to build some momentum.” ‘Mixtape’ co-host RJ Ochoa of Blogging the Boys obviously doesn’t want to see a Week 1 Giants’ victory. He also, though, acknowledged, what avoiding an 0-2 start could do for the retooled Giants. “A win against either one of these two teams, both games of which are on prime time, would establish a different feel, would establish a different level of belief.” A new era begins for the Giants next Sunday. Can they start it in a new way?
author: Ed Valentine

title: 2026 college football players to watch in Week 1 for the NY Giants
summary: Good morning New York Giants fans! Happy Saturday and welcome to Week 1 of the 2026 College Football Season. We’re actually already into the action of the 2026 college season, with Week 0 giving us some good games and surprising outcomes. But the real meat of the season starts today, and we have a full […]
full_text: Ole Miss defensive tackle Will Echoles rushes the Georgia quarterback.﻿ | Getty Images Good morning New York Giants fans! Happy Saturday and welcome to Week 1 of the 2026 College Football Season. We’re actually already into the action of the 2026 college season, with Week 0 giving us some good games and surprising outcomes. But the real meat of the season starts today, and we have a full slate of honest-to-goodness football action in store. So grab some snacks, pull up a seat, and let’s enjoy. As usual, we’ll be viewing the college game through the lens of the NFL Draft and focusing on games featuring prospects that could appeal to the Giants. I want to take that a step further this year and focus on prospects at positions of perceived need for the Giants. Right now, the positions I’m concentrating on are: Interior offensive line Wide receiver Interior defensive line Defensive back Of course, we’ll be updating our focus as the Giants’ season progresses. Needs can and will change as we wind our way through the season, with players stepping up or falling short of expectations. We’ll also get a much better idea of what the Giants’ offensive and defensive schemes look like, and what kinds of players they want. Now let’s get to the games! (3) Texas vs. Texas State ESPN – 3:30 p.m. Ryan Wingo, WR, Texas Ordinarily, this game wouldn’t draw much attention, though people will be turning in for Arch Manning. I don’t really expect it to be much of a competition, though I think Texas struggling would raise some red flags. Instead, I want to shine a light on a Texas wide receiver we may want to follow throughout the year. No, not Cam Coleman. If the Giants are in a position to draft Coleman, something has gone terribly wrong with either the Giants or Coleman. I want to point out Texas’ other receiver who’s garnering first round buzz: Ryan Wingo. Wingo is a big-bodied receiver at 6-foot-2, 215 pounds with a huge catch radius as well as impressive body control and ball skills. Wingo also has the potential to be a deep threat on the outside, with a background in track and (reported) 4.4 speed. As with a lot of the positions we’ll be focusing on this year, the Giants have real questions at wide receiver going forward. We don’t know what the future holds for Darius Slayton, Darnell Mooney, Calvin Austin, or Odell Beckham Jr. Likewise, we don’t know if Malachi Fields will live up to his training camp hype once teams start game planning for the Giants’ offense. Wide receiver could be fine, or it could be a real issue heading into the 2027 off-season. (11) LSU vs. Clemson ABC – 7:30 p.m. Dashawn Spears, S, LSU / Ashton Hampton, CB, Clemson I’m going to save some time and use one game to highlight two players — That’s the advantage of having two big programs play each other. This is the marquee game of the weekend, with a ton of drama and storylines. Will Clemson recover after a disastrous 2025 campaign or will Dabo be on the hot seat? What will LSU look like under Lane Kiffin? It’s early, but it feels like this game could determine if either has a shot at the College Football Playoffs. The Giants might be fine, or even good, in the secondary for 2026. But they also have long term questions that they’ll need to answer. Starting with the cornerback position, Deonte Banks and Greg Newsome II are on one-year deals. Paulson Adebo, meanwhile, could be a cap casualty. Likewise, the team will need to make a decision on SLOT/STAR Dru Phillips. That’s where Clemson cornerback Ashton Hampton comes in. Hampton has (potential) first-round traits as a big and long corner at roughly 6-foot-2, 205 pounds, and he plays up to his size. He also appears to have foot quickness and fluidity to stick in phase with receivers as a man corner. The Giants likely want to run an aggressive match quarters system and Hampton could be a player to watch if they feel the need to add a “number one” corner. Flipping over to the LSU side of things we have Dashawn Spears. Spears is (likewise) a big safety at roughly 6-foot-3, 210 pounds. In fact, Spears looks like the kind of player who teams might have encouraged to grow into a WILL linebacker in an earlier era. Now, however, he has a niche waiting as a downhill safety who’s a plus run defender while also having solid instincts and ball skills. The Giants also have a decision to make on Tyler Nubin while Ar’Darius Washington and Jason Pinnock are on one-year deals. One thing to keep in mind is that the “Ravens 2.0” school of defense loves to have a big and versatile safeties (such as Kyle Hamilton, Nick Emmanwori, and Derwin James) to change looks and dictate to the offense. (9) Ole Miss vs. (24) Louisville Sunday, Sept.6 ABC – 7:30 p.m. Will Echoles, iDL, Ole Miss This game isn’t until Sunday night, taking advantage of the break between the NFL’s preseason and regular season. But it’s a good thing that it has some room on the schedule to shine — after all, this is the only game between ranked teams on the schedule this week. The big story of the game will be the return of Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who fought to return to college football rather than go to the NFL. Chambliss is a much more advanced quarterback than many give him credit, and he should be a real factor in the 2027 Draft. But for our purposes, I want to look to the defensive side of the ball and defensive tackle Will Echoles. Echoles is a good-sized defensive tackle at roughly 6-foot-3, 315 pounds with great thickness in his upper and lower halves. He has traits and tools for days with obvious power, great explosiveness, and surprising movement skills for a big man. That said, he’s also only just scratching the surface of what he can become at just 20 years old (his birthday is August 7th). Echoles needs to refine his technique as his body continues to mature, but he’s already a difference maker on the Ole Miss defensive line. He’s a stout run defender who plays with great strength and motor, as well as a disruptor in the passing game. He finished last year with 5.0 sacks and also understands when to get his hands up to clog passing lanes if he can’t get to the QB. This looks like a great year for defensive tackles, and Echoles could earn a place among the best in the class.
author: Chris Pflum

title: New York Giants mailbag: Joe Schoen, Evan Neal, Jalin Hyatt, practice squad, more
summary: Brian Misdom asks: While this is older news, the season is quickly upon us and makes me wonder why the giants decided to extend Schoen before seeing any results on the field. It seemed premature – wouldn’t it have been prudent to see the fruits of the Harbaugh/Schoen pairing first? I just don’t see a […]
full_text: Brian Misdom asks: While this is older news, the season is quickly upon us and makes me wonder why the giants decided to extend Schoen before seeing any results on the field. It seemed premature – wouldn’t it have been prudent to see the fruits of the Harbaugh/Schoen pairing first? I just don’t see a lame duck GM as having the same distraction as a lame duck HC typically brings. Was there a real risk to our personnel operation if this wasn’t done over the summer? Ed says: Brian, Giants ownership has always liked the front office and scouting operation Schoen has put together. They have liked, as far as I can ascertain, how he communicates with ownership. Those things are important. The working relationship with Harbaugh is, of course, also incredibly important. By all accounts, the two have found common ground and an ability to work together. The fruits of that were shown in the Giants having what they felt was a fruitful offseason, both in the way they approached free agency and the draft. Harbaugh has talked about having the ability to “agree to agree” with the front office when he was in Baltimore. He has found that with Schoen. I think even the trades made in the week prior to the 53-man roster cut down show an ability for coach and GM to work together to build the roster the coach is looking for. The Giants liked what they saw in the relationship. Harbaugh was on board. Ownership saw no reason to make Schoen twist in the wind and keep answering questions about his job security. I am OK with that. Jimmy Siegel asks: Now that Evan Neal is in the rear view mirror, my question is what was it that Schoen and company didn’t see in the endless college film they no doubt dissected for months? I’ve always thought offensive lineman is one of the more easy transitions from college to pro. I believe that most first round OL tend to at least be quality starters in the NFL. But here’s a guy who let speed rushes fly by him like a turnstile. How was that missed by the Giants brain trust. Is the gap between speed rushers in college and the NFL that wide that it’s impossible to judge a college player? And yes, I know most teams had Neal as a top ten talent. So maybe my question should be what did the entire NFL miss with Neal? Ed says: Jimmy, I know that Joe Schoen has asked himself what, if anything, the Giants missed in their evaluation of Evan Neal. I know that he has gone back and studied the tape again. I also know that after re-watching that tape Schoen did not feel the Giants missed in their evaluation. He still believes he saw a player who, based on his college tape and what was known about him, deserved to be a top 10 pick. You are also right that most teams and talent evaluators agreed with Schoen, and that the pick was universally praised when the Giants made it. When I saw your question I went back and looked at a half-dozen or so pre-draft scouting reports on Neal. Almost everyone who evaluated him saw Neal as a future Pro Bowl or All-Pro caliber tackle. Evaluating players is not an exact science. I would disagree that the transition from college to NFL is easy for offensive linemen. College offensive linemen can be extremely difficult to evaluate. They often play little in a three-point stance. Many are hardly ever asked to run block. Many play in quick-passing offense that don’t ask them to do more than get in the way of a rusher for a second or so. Even at Alabama, Neal probably only squared up with real NFL talent two or three times each season. Evaluators knew there were a couple of issues with his pass protection, but felt those could/would be cleaned up with reps and NFL coaching. It didn’t happen. Why? Injuries? Coaching? The player himself? Being used at the wrong position? Nobody really knows. It is probably some combination of everything. It just didn’t work out. Daniel Frankel asks: For years I have felt that Harry Carson’s #53 deserved to be retired. I never enjoyed watching anyone else wear it. Now that Darius Muasau has been cut, do you think it would be a good time to retire The Captain’s number or at least to give that number to someone worthy of wearing the number, like Arvell Reese. Ed says: Daniel, the older I get the more I think numbers shouldn’t get retired in the first place. It gets a little silly after a while, and now we have numbers getting unretired so kids coming out of college who haven’t earned it yet can wear the number that goes with their brand. But, now that I’ve had my “get off my lawn” moment, if we are going to retire numbers then Harry Carson’s number should be among them. I don’t know why it has not been retired. The problem you run into in football, though, is that you run out of available jersey numbers. Still, Carson deserves that honor. Ed Helinski asks: Please describe the various amounts of money that practice squad players make? What kind of latitude do NFL teams have with deals for practice squad players? Might some be guaranteed deals? And how does the game check change when a player is elevated to the active roster? Ed says: Ed, the practice squad salaries are collectively bargained. The standard practice squad contract pays $13,750 per week. Teams can have up to six players who are “veterans”, designated as having two or more accrued seasons. Those players can earn a minimum of $18,350 per week and a maximum of $22,850. That’s it. There are no “guaranteed” practice squad deals. It is a week-to-week existence. Now, some undrafted free agents, like offensive tackle Ryan Schernecke, get guaranteed money when they sign. Schernecke received $247,500 guaranteed, which equates to a full season’s practice squad salary. Players elevated to a game day roster get the minimum pro-rated game day check for that week based on their experience level. Donald Leichter asks: Given the Giants’ obvious need for more run-stopping depth at defensive tackle, were you surprised they made no waiver claims despite having the No. 5 priority? Do you think they’re satisfied with the current group, or have you heard anything suggesting they’re pursuing a veteran run-stopper through a trade or free agency? Ed says: Donald, yes I was surprised they did not try to claim anyone. I do believe they would have made a claim or two if players they wanted had been there. Part of the process throughout the summer is identifying players you would like to claim if they are cut by other teams. I know that in the past the Giants have said there were players they wanted who ended up being kept by their teams rather than released. I would think that happened here, as well. As much as they know there are a few spots that need upgrading, they likely felt that what was available was not better than what they had. Matthew Sanzone asks: Questions from a practice squad dummy: 1. Do PS players travel with the team to away games? 2. Are they provided per diem money for expenses such as meals? 3. Do they have medical insurance as part of their compensation? Ed says: Matthew, let’s look at each of these. There is no set answer to that. Practice squad players who are going to play travel, of course. In some instances, they will travel as a reward. In many instances, they will not. Remember, that is 15 or so extra people to put on an airplace already filled with large people. Practice squad players get free access to meals provided at team facilities. If they are traveling with the team, they are treated like everyone else. Practice squad players get medical benefits. Here is a look from a few years ago at those benefits . Pat Lam asks: Adding Jalin Hyatt to the practice squad is a headscratcher. Do you have any insight as to why? Ed says: Pat, Hyatt was injured when the Giants were still in West Virginia and missed the rest of training camp and the entire preseason. He had been making some plays in practice, and the Giants were giving him an opportunity as a punt gunner. Perhaps the Giants feel like the injury, caused by an overzealous hit from a…

title: NY Giants news: Skattebo’s relationship with Harbaugh, top ESPN players, more news
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories as you start you Labor Day Weekend. Gauging John Harbaugh’s impact and what to expect in Week 1 | The Athletic Harbaugh has brought credibility to the organization. No one knows if this will ultimately work. Plenty of accomplished coaches have flamed out at later […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories as you start you Labor Day Weekend. Gauging John Harbaugh’s impact and what to expect in Week 1 | The Athletic Harbaugh has brought credibility to the organization. No one knows if this will ultimately work. Plenty of accomplished coaches have flamed out at later stops. But no other coach on the market this offseason could have generated this level of buy-in. A leader with a clear vision is leading the organization. Everyone believes in Harbaugh’s methods because he can point to his lengthy track record of success. The Giants feel like a professional organization for the first time in a long time. How that translates to wins and losses remains to be seen, but Harbaugh’s impact has already been profound. To Harbaugh’s credit: confidence. It used to drive me crazy at this time of year when general manager Joe Schoen and former coach Brian Daboll always ran from any expectation of winning games. That’s what made Harbaugh’s comments Wednesday about expecting to win so refreshing. Surely there has to be some anxiety about starting this new journey with a roster that clearly has flaws. But Harbaugh and the players seem genuinely eager to get started. Is Jihad Ward coming back to the Giants? View this post on Instagram 2026 NFL season X factors: Key players for all 32 teams | ESPN.com DT DJ Reader. Reader was once a premier run-stuffing nose tackle in this league, but his numbers are down over the past two seasons. His stop rate of 8.6% last season — the percentage of tackles that stopped the run for negative expected points, per NFL Next Gen Stats — was his lowest single-season mark since 2018. His stuff rate of 1.1% — the percentage of tackles that were for zero or fewer yards — was the lowest of his career. The splashy impact against the run is waning for the 32-year-old. How many snaps does Reader have in him at his age, and can he achieve more impact against the run in a new defensive system in New York? Without a renaissance Reader season, I’m worried that we’ll see another season in which the Giants’ defense is too easy to run on for its pass rush to really matter. Agent’s Take: Does Cam Skattebo need better advice after recent Giants antics? | CBSSports.com When situations like these arise, an agent should provide counsel to their client. It’s an agent’s job to tell a client what he needs to hear, not what he wants to hear. That isn’t always done. Some agents are reluctant to be candid for fear of being fired and instead become enablers. Skattebo plays in the United States’ biggest media market, so any missteps are more magnified in New York. The good news for Skattebo is that the regular-season opener against the Dallas Cowboys is less than two weeks away. The attention will primarily be on how he performs in his return from the injury. If Skattebo can pick up from where he left off last season, then anything relating to the offseason or preseason will just be a minor blip on the radar screen in the grander scheme of things. The Giants lineage and Ice Bowl pedigree Ben Mann brings as he tries to write his own Big Blue story | New York Post It is probably a bit of hyperbole to suggest Ben Mann was born to be a Giant. But there is Giants lineage coursing through his veins and NFL pedigree in his genes and there is a close family link that takes this otherwise nondescript 24-year-old — he’s a long snapper, for goodness’ sake — and vaults him into a space where few have entered. Method to the madness: Reason why Giants limited recording at practice | USAToday.com Entities are entitled to their “corporate secrets,” and the Giants are no different. Under new head coach John Harbaugh, there is much less media and fan access to practices, to the point where video, pictures, and the description of the action aren’t flowing freely on social media for the world to consume. Some teams haven’t clamped down as hard yet, though. In a recent press conference, Miami Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley admitted that he has fallen victim to fans posting videos of his practices and other teams using that footage against him. title: Ex-New York Jets Progress Report: Part I (Offense)
summary: With rosters set, it’s a good time to keep track of where any former Jets have ended up and what their role will be in 2026. We will cover this over three parts, looking at offensive and defensive players this week and special teamers next week. As ever, this list is intended to be exhaustive, […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 28: Quarterback Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks warms up prior to the preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images With rosters set, it’s a good time to keep track of where any former Jets have ended up and what their role will be in 2026. We will cover this over three parts, looking at offensive and defensive players this week and special teamers next week. As ever, this list is intended to be exhaustive, but if we missed anyone, let us know in the comments. Commanders: Washington cuts ties with tight end Lawrence Cager, but did sign tackle Esa Pole to their practice squad after he was cut by the Chiefs. Cowboys: The only ex-Jet retained by Dallas on offense was running back Israel Abanikanda, who is on the practice squad. They cut ties with a handful more: Offensive lineman Chris Glaser, wide receivers Tyler Johnson and Denzel Mims and tight end Zack Kuntz. Eagles: Tight end EJ Jenkins and wide receiver Elijah Moore both made the final roster, as Moore in particular seems to have responded well to another fresh start. Giants: The Giants had 10 ex-Jets on the team, mostly on defense. They cut wide receivers Xavier Gipson and Braxton Berrios despite Gipson’s touchdown in the final preseason game against the Jets. Berrios was re-signed to the practice squad even though he lost a fumble in that game. Packers: As expected, quarterback Tyrod Taylor won the backup role, as the Packers retained just two quarterbacks on their 53. Vikings: Minnesota didn’t have any ex-Jets on offense during the offseason. Bears: Chicago retained wide receiver Kalif Raymond on their active roster, although he didn’t play for them at all in preseason. Lions: The only ex-Jet to end up on Detroit’s roster was tight end Tyler Conklin , who was actually cut initially but then re-signed the next day. They had several others, none of whom were retained on the practice squad: Wide receivers Greg Dortch and Tarik Black, tight ends Nick Muse and Anthony Firkser and offensive lineman Gus Hartwig. Quarterback Teddy Bridgewater opted to retire again. Bucs: Guard Dan Feeney was retained on the main roster, although he’s listed as the backup at center. Saints: Quarterback Zach Wilson made New Orleans’ roster but he’s listed as the number three behind Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler. Wilson was 20 of 28 for 238 yards and a touchdown, with no interceptions, in preseason. The Saints also added tight end Stone Smartt to their practice squad. Panthers: Carolina retained former Jets receiver John Metchie III on their roster after he caught seven passes for 82 yards in preseason. Falcons: Offensive lineman Corey Levin made the Falcons roster in a backup role. They also picked Muse up for their practice squad after his release from the Lions. Quarterback Trevor Siemian was released before preseason got underway with a non-football injury. Rams: Wide receiver Davante Adams should have a big role for the Rams again, and he was just named as a team captain. The Rams cut offensive lineman Blake Hance but re-signed him to their practice squad. Seahawks: Super Bowl MVP quarterback Sam Darnold will obviously be back for Seattle this year. They also currently still have wide receiver Irv Charles on injured reserve but he’s expected to be activated at some point. Cardinals: Running back Bam Knight managed to make the roster, although tight end Kenny Yeboah was cut. Knight, who rushed 15 times for 75 yards in preseason, will be the third running back until James Conner comes off injured reserve. 49ers: The 49ers didn’t keep either of their offensive players that used to be Jets, as both quarterback Adrian Martinez and running back Khalil Herbert were cut and not signed to the practice squad. Bills: Running back Ty Johnson is back once again as Buffalo’s third down back. The Bills also had three ex-Jets wideouts on their team: Mecole Hardman, Mac Dalena and Quentin Skinner. However, after cutting all three, they opted to sign a fourth ex-Jet, Dortch, to the practice squad ahead of any of them following his release from the Lions. Dolphins: In a surprise move, Miami claimed Jets quarterback Brady Cook off waivers, so he’s currently on their 53-man roster. Running back Donovan Edwards was not retained and offensive lineman Carter Warren is on injured reserve. Patriots: The Patriots had four ex-Jets and all four made the final roster. Three were on offense, all on the line. Alijah Vera-Tucker , Morgan Moses and Greg Van Roten all started together in the first half of the 2021 season on the Jets, but Van Roten will be coming off the bench behind Mike Onwenu. Bengals: Faced with a choice of two ex-Jets, Cincinnati opted to go with Joe Flacco as their backup quarterback and signed Josh Johnson to the practice squad. Browns: Wide receiver Malachi Corley only caught two passes in preseason but Cleveland saw enough to keep him on the roster. Tight end Brenden Bates was cut. Ravens: John Simpson will start for the Ravens at left guard as expected. They also signed running back Jonathan Ward to the practice squad. Steelers: Quarterback Aaron Rodgers is back at the helm in Pittsburgh, but they cut two ex-Jets receivers in Isaiah Winstead and Brandon Smith. Smith was re-signed to the practice squad. Texans: Brett Rypien was the only ex-Jets offensive player on the Texans this offseason and he wasn’t retained. Colts: Wide receiver DJ Montgomery was a late addition for the Colts but he ended up on injured reserve with an abdomen issue. Titans: Robert Saleh had an incredible 14 ex-Jets on his roster over the offseason and retained nine, albeit that four of those are on the practice squad and one on injured reserve. Only four of these 14 players were on offense, and all four of those were cut, although running back Michael Carter and quarterback Hendon Hooker made the practice squad. Offensive lineman Austin Deculus and wideout Lance McCutcheon were not retained. Jaguars: The Jaguars had two ex-Jets on their offensive line but neither made the final roster as Trystan Colon retired and Chuma Edoga was a surprise cut. Edoga basically didn’t play during preseason, leading Jags writers to assume he was safe. Broncos: Wide receiver Tarik Black was the only ex-Jet on Denver’s roster this offseason but he didn’t last long and ended up on the Lions. Chargers: The Chargers didn’t have any ex-Jets on offense this offseason. Raiders: Tight end Zack Kuntz was briefly with the Raiders but he ended up in Dallas. Chiefs: Quarterback Justin Fields will back up a now-healthy Patrick Mahomes after completing 13 of 16 passes in preseason. Offensive tackle Esa Pole and wide receiver Jason Brownlee were both waived. Pole was picked up by Washington and Brownlee wasn’t kept on the practice squad. We’ll be back with a look at defensive players in a day or two.

title: Predicting the Jets Opening Day Lineup
summary: We’re finally back. New York Jets football is about a week away. Gang Green returns to the field with higher expectations than they’ve had in the past. That’s not to say that anyone expects them to be a good football team, but they do have some expectations. With Frank Reich leading the offense, and a […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - AUGUST 14: Armand Membou #70 of the New York Jets lines up during the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at MetLife Stadium on August 14, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Evan Bernstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re finally back. New York Jets football is about a week away. Gang Green returns to the field with higher expectations than they’ve had in the past. That’s not to say that anyone expects them to be a good football team, but they do have some expectations. With Frank Reich leading the offense, and a talented Offensive Line and group of skill position players, the Jets offense should be fun for the first time in a long time. The Jets have not had an offense ranked outside the bottom-10 in scoring in the league since 2015. While the offense certainly won’t compete with the best in the league, avoiding a bottom 10 mark in the league feels like it should be very attainable for this group. Meanwhile, the Jets focus this offseason was almost all on the defensive side. Head Coach Aaron Glenn is going to call plays again, after yielding that responsibility in his first year. The Jets spent nearly all of their money in free agency on the defensive side of the ball. Not to mention they used the #2 pick and a 2nd round pick on premium defensive positions. Neither Glenn nor General Manager Darren Mougey can afford for the defense to be anything near as bad as it was last season. So who are the players that will lead this team with modest expectations? Let’s take a look at the expected starting lineup in Week 1 agains the Tennessee Titans. Offense QB: Geno Smith The former Jets second round pick is back for his second stint with the franchise. Smith found success as a starter in his career with the Seahawks, but a disastrous stint last year with the Las Vegas Raiders left many speculating that the soon to be 36-year old quarterback is at the end of his career. However, Smith dealt with a horrible situation last year. He had Chip Kelly as his offensive coordinator, the NFL’s fifth-worst pass blocking offensive line, per PFF grade, arguably the NFL’s worst WR group, and a severely unperforming top-10 pick in Ashton Jeanty at RB. Smith comes into a much better situation here with Reich as his offensive coordinator, an above average OL, an above average RB, and a WR room that if nothing else has a true WR1. Will that be enough to get him back to how he looked in Seattle? I Ccn’t say for sure, but Aaron Glenn is certainly betting on it. RB: Breece Hall Breece Hall needs no introduction. He’s one of the best skill position players in Jets history. He’s second in team history in yards from scrimmage per game, behind only Hall of Famer Curtis Martin. He averages over 1,500 yards per 17 games. He’s a threat both in the backfield and as a receiver. He’s a home run hitter, even if he may not be the most efficient runner in the league. If the Jets offense is going to take off this year, Hall will be a big reason for it. One thing to keep an eye on though is how often Hall is used in the passing game. The last two Jets offensive coordinators underutilized Hall, only to admit that was a mistake as the season went on. Hall hasn’t featured much in the passing game in practice this year with Smith only targeting him three times all camp according to Zack Rosenblatt . WR: Garrett Wilson, AD Mitchell, and Isaiah Williams Garrett Wilson is a true WR1 in this league. He suffered from injuries last season that limited him to by far the worst season of his career. He’s an easy bounceback candidate for the Jets. AD Mitchell is someone the Jets are incredibly high on. Reports all offseason have come that Mitchell and Smith have great chemsitry that could turn into a breakout season for the former second round pick. However, Mitchell is very unproven entering his third year. I’m going with Isaiah Williams as the expected starter in the slot. He had a better camp and better preseason than Omar Cooper. Williams was also named a team captain. That said, I’d expect Cooper to get a ton of reps, and I wouldn’t be surprised if he does in fact start over Williams. TE: Mason Taylor Mason Taylor had a great camp and preseason, really establishing himself as Smith’s safety blanket. Look for Taylor to be Smith’s first option on short yardage plays and against zone. He’s got great hands and finds soft spots in the defense easily. He just lacks the athleticism to be anything more. That’s where Kenyon Sadiq comes in, who likely would have been the opening day starter had he been healthy. However, he missed all of the offseason and camp due to injury after hernia surgery. It looks like he’s going to be ready to take the field to start the season, as he’s been practicing ahead of the game. However, that missed time is going to be hard to make up. Expect a slow start from the rookie. Offensive Line: Olu Fashanu, Dylan Parham, Josh Myers, Joe Tippmann, and Armand Membou Olu Fashanu made a nice jump last year. He finished as the Jets best pass blocking offensive lineman per PFF grade. He still struggles in the run game, and that’s where he needs to make a big improvement this season. Still, if he stagnates, at least the Jets can go to sleep at night knowing they have a legitmate left tackle. After all, Olu finished with a 69.2 grade last season, that was 17th among the left tackles who played at least 50% of their team’s snaps. From Week 7 to the end of the year, Olu was 17th among all tackles in total grade. Parham was the Jets lone starter on offense acquired via free agency. Signing a two year, $20 million contract this offseason, Parham steps in at LG to replace John Simpson. He was part of that horrible Raiders offensive line last season. He gave up six sacks, the second most of any guard in the NFL. His 63.5 grade was 32nd of the 61 guards who played at least 50% of their team snaps last year. The hope is that was a blip, as Parham was much better the year before when his 74.3 grade was 17th among all guards who played at least 50% of snaps. Josh Myers returns as the center after a disappointing season in 2025. He was the clear weak link in the Jets offensive line, grading out as second worst center in the league to play at least 50% of snaps. He gave up the third most sacks and the third most pressures from the position, and he was among the worst run blockers. Jets are hoping for major improvement here. Joe Tippmann was named a captain this season. He enters his second full season as a guard in the NFL. He struggled with the transition early last season, but came into his own as the season went on. From Weeks 10-18 last season, Tippmann was 10th among all guards in pass block grade. He was also called for just one penalty over the final six games of the season. Armand Membou is the Jets most talented offensive lineman. A stud out of the gate, Membou was a league average right tackle as a rookie. He’s shown again this offseason that he has the talent to be an All-Pro. The question for the second year man is if he can take that leap in real games this season. Defense EDGE: David Bailey and Kingsley Enagbare David Bailey was a lock to be here as soon as the Jets used the second pick in this April’s draft on him. The former Texas Tech superstar comes in with high expectations as a pass rusher, and he’s looked every bit that good in camp. Bailey is going to need to prove his worth quickly, as his pass rushing skill is his only dominant skill. He has a known weakness against the run. Opposite him will be free agent addition Kingsley Enagbare. The former Packer had a standout camp while Joseph Ossai was injured. As a result he has leapfrogged Will McDonald on the depth chart and likely earned the Week 1 start. This will be the first time Enagbare is a starter in his NFL career. The most snaps he’s ever played in a single season before is 509. He’s been used as a heavy rotation player, but never the main guy. Over his career, Enagbare has just a…

summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! It’s easier to buy a bounce back season from Cam Jurgens (although back injuries are never comforting) than it is from Landon Dickerson. Jurgens looks healthy and sounds excited for the new season. Dickerson reportedly gave consideration to retirement after 2025 […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - DECEMBER 15: Cam Jurgens #51 and Landon Dickerson #69 of the Philadelphia Eagles in action against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Lincoln Financial Field on December 15, 2024 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! It’s easier to buy a bounce back season from Cam Jurgens (although back injuries are never comforting) than it is from Landon Dickerson. Jurgens looks healthy and sounds excited for the new season. Dickerson reportedly gave consideration to retirement after 2025 (although he denied as much) and he looked physically diminished at times during camp. That being said, we did see positive signs from the running game in training camp. We’ll see if it carries over to game action. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … 2026 NFL season X factors: Key players for all 32 teams – ESPN LG Landon Dickerson and C Cam Jurgens. There are many directions to go with the Eagles. Dontayvion Wicks is the clear WR2 after never really cracking WR4 with the Packers. Can he be a consistent veteran presence in A.J. Brown’s absence? Edge Jonathan Greenard is stepping in for Jaelan Phillips, who was a huge force multiplier for the defense last season. A pec injury forced Greenard to sit out all of training camp, which begs the question: Is he ready to go in the new system? But I’m circling the duo of Dickerson and Jurgens here. The Eagles’ left guard and center — both in the top five highest-paid players at their respective positions — were shells of themselves last season because of lingering injuries. Jurgens had back issues so intense that he had to go to Colombia for stem-cell treatment. Dickerson had a right meniscus tear, a back injury and multiple ankle injuries. He, too, joined Jurgens in Colombia for stem-cell therapy. The Eagles’ running game suffered dramatically as Philadelphia’s two core interior players labored with nagging injuries. On running back carries (i.e., not tush pushes and other QB runs), the Eagles averaged only 1.2 yards before contact per carry after producing 2.0 the season previous — almost half as good of a run-blocking unit as it had been. No matter the new schemes and clever tricks of offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, the Eagles’ offense was Super Bowl-caliber only when the running game was shredding behind an elite offensive line. Dickerson and Jurgens must truly be healthy if we’re to see that version of the Eagles again, and that makes them Philly’s biggest X factor of all. The Eagles’ trendsetting roster – BGN There are over 500 players on practice squads and over 600 players who were in a camp that are currently free agents (or on LSU’s roster). If you need another backup running back, slot receiver, slot corner, off ball LB, there’s plenty lying around. The Eagles problem isn’t that they have 4 QBs. Their problem is that one who is second on the depth chart is a washed up Andy Dalton. Roob’s Observations: How good can Saquon be at an age when most RBs are fading? – NBCSP WHAT TO EXPECT FROM SAQUON: Saquon Barkley had a terrific training camp and it sure looks like he’s primed for a big bounce-back year in Sean Mannion’s offense after an up-and-down 2025 in a miserable offense behind a banged-up offensive line. But he’s also 29, and that’s an age where running backs historically are going downhill. In the last 20 years, only four running backs have rushed for 1,300 yards after turning 29 – Thomas Jones twice with the Jets, Michael Turner with the Falcons, Adrian Peterson once and Derrick Henry twice. Now, Barkley takes such good care of himself and looked so locked in during camp and seems like such a natural fit in this scheme, I don’t see any reason he can’t rush for 1,500 yards if he plays all 17 games. Only nine backs have ever rushed for 1,500 yards after turning 29, only Henry in the last 20 years. But I don’t care what the history is or what the numbers say. I’ll be surprised if Saquon isn’t in that ballpark by the time we get to January. He’s still that good. Eagles mailbag: What backup could end up starting by season’s end? – PhillyVoice I think that there’s an argument that Trotter is a better player, right now, because he has had more time in the scheme, he understands where he needs to be, he can anticipate where the ball is going, and he has Vic Fangio’s trust. However, if he is better, it’s marginal at best. Jihaad Campbell is a far more gifted player in terms of size and athleticism and the only way he is going to get better is if he plays. Their respective ceilings aren’t close. Campbell has All-Pro potential. Trotter does not. So Campbell (rightfully) is going to play. If Campbell is just bad for some reason and he is making losing plays, could they make a switch? Sure, but I think they’ll be patient there, and in my opinion Campbell played well enough as a rookie that there’s little reason to anticipate that he’ll falter. The spot that I would look at is LG. If Landon Dickerson gets banged up again like he did in 2025 and his body simply won’t cooperate, I do think it’s possible that a fresh Drew Kendall could fill in and be a better player. But also, if any of the three starting interior linemen go down, Kendall will be the first guy off the bench. He’s easily the top backup candidate to start games this season. Super Bowl LXI predictions: Los Angeles Rams lead seven NFL favorites to hoist Lombardi Trophy – NFL.com Ben McWilliams: Eagles over Bills. Joe Brady helps Josh Allen get over the hump, but the Bills fall short in the Super Bowl to an Eagles team led by an elite defense. Once a wish kid herself, this Eagles Cheerleader now makes wishes come true – PhiladelphiaEagles.com The Eagles and Make-A-Wish thought they were hosting five wish kids to play mini-golf with Jalen Hurts last week. As it turns out, there were actually six wish kids at the event. Three Eagles Cheerleaders went to spend time with the wish kids and their families. Among them was Jordyn, a rookie cheerleader who had just made her debut to fans at Public Practice. Once a wish kid herself, Jordyn found herself on the other side of the Make-A-Wish experience, making sure the kids’ and families’ day was special. “It was honestly a really surreal experience,” Jordyn said. “I really felt like I was living two lives in that moment. It was truly an honor to be there with those kids and be there for them that day.” “It really was one of the best days of my life.” A native of Richboro, Pennsylvania, Jordyn was diagnosed with kidney cancer at only 3 years old. When she became part of the Make-A-Wish family, the cheerleader-to-be asked to go to Disney World. Raiders’ Patrick Johnson a feel-good story, but veteran earned his spot – Silver And Black Pride Johnson, who entered the league and spent the majority of is NFL career with the Philadelphia Eagles as a seventh-round pick (234th overall) in the 2021 NFL Draft, tops Slone in experience and and gameday production this preseason. And has the mentality required for NFL longshots as he was a July 27 signing by the Raiders — Slone in comparison was inked as an UDFA back on April 30. Rams Cut DB Zech McPhearson From Injured Reserve – NFL Trade Rumors The Los Angeles Rams officially released DB Zech McPhearson from injured reserve with an injury settlement on Saturday. McPhearson, 28, is a former fourth-round pick of the Eagles back in 2021. He signed a four-year rookie contract with Philadelphia following the draft. If the Cowboys lose their franchise quarterback for an extended amount of time, that’s bad news, and we’re all well aware of that. That means every year we hold our breath that Dak Prescott doesn’t get hurt. At 33 years old, he’s no longer a spring chicken, meaning his body doesn’t respond the same way, and certain ailments can…

title: The Eagles’ trendsetting roster
summary: The Eagles roster is, in theory set for Week 1, though there is still plenty of time to make changes. Unintentionally, their roster construction led the way. Howie Roseman does it again! Fantastic 4 QBs There has been some consternation about teams carrying 4 QBs on their 53 man roster this year: the Eagles, Steelers, […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 28: Philadelphia Eagles executive vice president and general manager Howie Roseman looks on before the pre season game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Cincinnati Bengals on August 28th, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Eagles roster is, in theory set for Week 1, though there is still plenty of time to make changes. Unintentionally, their roster construction led the way. Howie Roseman does it again! Fantastic 4 QBs There has been some consternation about teams carrying 4 QBs on their 53 man roster this year: the Eagles, Steelers, Falcons, Vikings, and Browns all had four on their initial 53 man roster, though since then the Browns put Dillon Gabriel on IR and the Vikings cut Max Brosmer and re-signed him to the practice squad. This is no big deal. Teams have always used the bottom of their rosters to store either big, raw athletes (usually linemen, sometimes WRs or TEs) or QBs because those types of players are rare. And those types of players are rare because teams have always used the bottom of their rosters to store big, raw athletes or QBs. It’s a bit of a self fulfilling prophecy. Brady Cook got claimed. To use another Brady on the other end of the scale, in his rookie season Tom Brady was the 4th QB on a 5-11 team. There are over 500 players on practice squads and over 600 players who were in a camp that are currently free agents (or on LSU’s roster). If you need another backup running back, slot receiver, slot corner, off ball LB, there’s plenty lying around. The Eagles problem isn’t that they have 4 QBs. Their problem is that one who is second on the depth chart is a washed up Andy Dalton. 4 on the roster floor That said, the Eagles did have, in a weird coincidence, 4 players claimed by other teams, the most of any team. Is that a sign that the team is deep, or a sign that they may have cut some players they shouldn’t have? Last year the Chargers, Rams, and Ravens led the way with three players claimed by other teams. The Chargers got hit with injuries and still won 11 games, the Rams won 12, and the Ravens had injury problems of their own and won 8 games. In 2024 the 49ers and Packers also had three. The Packers won 11 games while the 49ers got obliterated by injuries and went 6-11, which is a pretty good record for a team that started 3 different QBs and had half their starters miss at least 3 games. The Eagles QB, WR, and TE depth charts have issues, but the rest of this roster looks pretty good. College Football Watch List 12:00 – Boise State at Oregon Oregon is loaded. With Moro Ojomo scheduled to hit free agency in March, I’ve got my eye on DTs A’Mauri Washington , a run stuffer who needs to show better pass rush ability, and Bear Alexander , who has completely turned his career around (a weird thing to say about a college kid, but it’s true) with the Ducks. 7:30 – Clemson at LSU The only game between a ranked team and a Power 4 opponent on Saturday. It might be over by half time. LSU has a pair of EDGEs to watch. Princewill Umanmielen , brother of Princely, who had a breakout season at Ole Miss last year and followed Lane Kiffin to LSU. He needs to add to his repertoire but his size, length, and motor are really good. Jordan Ross is getting some buzz in the amateur scouting world. He was one of the top EDGE recruits in 2024 but spent two years in a situational role at Tennessee. Now he’s at LSU and should see regular playing time so long as Jack Pyburn is on the Chiefs. Clemson EDGE Will Heldt is one of the top senior prospects. Here in September he seems like a day two pick, but that might be too high. Sunday – 7:30 – Louisville at Ole Miss Trinidad Chambliss is getting way too much hype based off of two (very good) games last year. His draft stock probably won’t be higher than it was this offseason when he decided that a paycheck at Ole Miss was a better option (he was right). He’s a day three pick, and to me he feels like a Howie Roseman pick. Sunday – 7:30 – Wisconsin at Notre Dame Notre Dame has prospects all along the defense, and might have the best secondary in 2026. CB Leonard Moore is a top prospect, while CBs DJ McKinney and Christian Grey and safeties Tae Johnson and Adon Shuler are highly rated as well. Wisconsin is just trying to not get anyone fired this year. Monday – 7:30 – SMU at Florida State 6’7” FSU WR Johnny Wilson was a worthy gamble in the 6th round. It didn’t work out, but that’s the way it usually goes with gambles. Maybe 6’6” FSU WR Duce Robinson is worth a try.

title: Eagles News: NFL offense rankings have Philadelphia in the middle of the pack
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Ranking the Eagles as the 16th best offense in the NFL feels fair, in part because it’s hard to know exactly where to put them. The feeling here is that they won’t be consistently mediocre as must as we could see […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JULY 30: Cam Jurgens #51, Dallas Goedert #88, Saquon Barkley #26, and Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles look on during training camp at Jefferson Health Training Complex on July 30, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Ranking the Eagles as the 16th best offense in the NFL feels fair, in part because it’s hard to know exactly where to put them. The feeling here is that they won’t be consistently mediocre as must as we could see some ups and downs. I also tend to think that progress won’t be linear in this situation but one would hope they’ll be hitting their stride on offense by later in the season. What say you? Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Who Will Have the NFL’s Best Offense in 2026? – The Ringer 16) PHILADELPHIA EAGLES. The bottom fell out of the Eagles offense last year under former coordinator Kevin Patullo. It finished 19th in EPA per drive and had the fifth-highest three-and-out rate in the NFL. A combination of run blocking regression and a failure to provide any surprises in the passing game culminated in a wild-card exit and one of the most miserable 11-win seasons in NFL history. The offense will look entirely different under new offensive coordinator and first-time play caller Sean Mannion, who most recently coached under Matt LaFleur in Green Bay. The Eagles have to replace A.J. Brown, which they’ll attempt to do in the aggregate through Dontayvion Wicks and rookie Makai Lemon. There will be more snaps under center and more throws over the middle. They’ll ask Jalen Hurts to throw with anticipation more frequently, and how well he adapts to these changes will determine how the Eagles offense fares this season. It could be a breakout year for DeVonta Smith if things break right—and he’s been elite without Brown on the field—but there may well be growing pains for the Eagles as they attempt to adjust to a new offensive scheme and face sky-high expectations. Top 10 NFL offenses in 2026? Bears, Bills, Rams headline my projection – NFL.com The Eagles are not in the top 10 here. The Cowboys check in at No. 5. It’s not easy advancing deep into January without a top-tier offense these days. Last season, of the top 10 teams in offensive points per game (OPPG) — we’re talking points scored by the offense only (defensive and/or kick return scores not included) — seven made the playoffs. Six of the eight teams that played in the Divisional Round ranked among the top 10 in OPPG, as did the teams that met in the Super Bowl. Eagles announce 7 captains for the 2026 season – BGN Congrats to Jordan Davis, who is a first-time captain. No surprise there; he’s been an emerging leader on this team. That aspect is part of why the Eagles signed him to a long-term contract extension. What I’m Worried About – Iggles Blitz I mentioned Jalen Hurts as one of the things I’m excited to see. He also falls into the category of potential concerns. Hurts is learning a new offense and has new receivers to throw to. There are going to be some ups and downs. Hurts had some bad games in previous years, but he was always able to bounce back from them. Could all the new changes turn a bad game into multiple bad games? I think Hurts will be fine, but it is fair to acknowledge there could be real struggles. The passing game was erratic this summer. There are some reasons for that. Still, there are no guarantees things will go well. We will all be curious to see how Hurts plays this fall. Sean Mannion is a first time offensive coordinator. He’s stepped into a team with Super Bowl expectations. That is the standard in Philly these days. Mannion will have the pressure of dealing with rabid fans and one of the league’s biggest media contingents. He, and Hurts, will be living under a microscope. Everything we’ve heard about Mannion is promising, but he will have some ups and downs of his own. No new coordinator gets things perfect right away. You learn on the job. We’ll see how he handles Hurts, Nick Sirianni, fan pressure and media scrutiny. Mannion is getting ready to go one one heck of a roller coaster ride. 2026 NFL rookies guide: Stat leaders, fantasy picks, top QBs – ESPN 5) Makai Lemon, WR, Philadelphia Eagles. Philadelphia traded up to No. 20 for Lemon after he averaged 3.04 yards per route run in college and dropped just three of 190 career targets. With A.J. Brown gone, there are targets available, but Lemon still has to beat out Dontayvion Wicks for a bigger role. Lemon is a WR5 for now in fantasy leagues, with room to climb if he locks down the No. 2 job. A dozen records and milestones within reach with Eagles set to open 2026 season – NBCSP In just six NFL seasons, Jalen Hurts has rushed for 63 touchdowns and he needs seven to pass Steve Van Buren and set the franchise record. Van Buren rushed for 69 TDs in his eight-year career from 1944 through 1951. Hurts has 3,554 career rushing yards and needs 446 to become the seventh quarterback to reach 4,000 for his career. He would join Lamar Jackson (6,522), former Eagle Michael Vick (6,109), Cam Newton (5,628), Russell Wilson (5,568), former Eagle Randall Cunningham (4,928), Josh Allen (4,721) and Steve Young (4,239). Young Eagles starter has found ‘[his] legs’ after a shaky start: Why he’s in line for a big payday – NJ.com “I see a guy who’s been really, really consistent at his job this camp,” Kuper said about Steen on Thursday. “He’s probably been one of the most consistent guys on offense. He’s been there every day. He’s got a lot of power. He’s an athletic kid, and you just kind of see the game coming together for him a little bit. Takes time as a young player regardless. What is this? Year four for Tyler. It takes time to find your legs, to find your confidence.” After the Eagles cut Uar Bernard, a Delco bar threw a surprise party to help lift his spirits – Inquirer On Sunday, when the 53-man roster was announced, few took the news of Bernard’s cut harder than Damian. Bernard’s publicist, Adrian Fox, reached out to Aldridge and Damian to come out to the Jefferson Health Training Complex to lift Bernard’s spirits. It was then that Dolan had the idea of a pep rally at the bar to show Bernard what he’s come to mean to the city. “This bar’s been in business for 73 years, and I have rarely seen so much hype over somebody who’s never played a sport before, let alone just any player,” Dolan said. “The physical anomaly that he is, how grateful and humble the young man is, all of it.” Usually, Dolan would use social media to promote big events like this. But Fox told him Bernard is always on social media. Instead, the party had to be promoted the old-fashioned way: word of mouth. With connections to the city’s prominent sports social media figures and a “finger on that pulse,” Dolan said he was able to get word out. The only social media post he shared was a vague video of him telling followers to “trust” him that they’d want to be at the bar on Thursday night, reminding them to bring their “Birds gear.” Spadaro: For Eagles secondary, compliments are nice, but winning is what matters – PhiladelphiaEagles.com The preseason compliments are nice and everything, but Eagles Secondary Coach Mike Pellegrino takes them for what they are truly worth: A whole lot of not much. As the world heaps praise on the team’s trio of cornerback talents – led by All-Pro players Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean, along with first-year Eagle Riq Woolen – Pellegrino is taking a much more pragmatic approach. “I’ve always felt like the preseason expectations are great, that’s nice, but let’s see how we do when the ball is snapped. That’s always been my thing, because it’s a long season and you’re playing corner and you could be playing great 59 out of 60 plays, but everybody is going to be talking about that one play,” said Pellegrino, a coach with…

title: Former NFL lineman has major concerns about Steelers’ new-look O-line
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are entering the 2026 season with a revamped offensive line and a new offensive philosophy under head coach Mike McCarthy. According to former NFL center A.Q. Shipley, the transition could create some significant problems. Shipley, who spent 12 seasons in the NFL, joined The Pat McAfee Show this week to discuss Pittsburgh’s offensive line […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 28: Troy Fautanu #76 of the Pittsburgh Steelers in cation during the second quarter against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on December 28, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are entering the 2026 season with a revamped offensive line and a new offensive philosophy under head coach Mike McCarthy. According to former NFL center A.Q. Shipley, the transition could create some significant problems. Shipley, who spent 12 seasons in the NFL, joined The Pat McAfee Show this week to discuss Pittsburgh’s offensive line and expressed concern about how the group will adapt to McCarthy’s system. “I’m concerned about the Steelers offensive line,” he said. “I think they’re going to take a step back.” "I'm concerned about the Steelers offensive line.. I think they're gonna take a step back" @aqshipley #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/nSF8hA5od2 — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) September 1, 2026 Shipley believes the issue goes beyond individual talent. Instead, he pointed to the schematic transition from former offensive coordinator Arthur Smith to McCarthy as a potentially significant challenge. “Scheme and fit are everything,” he said. “I think they were built to run in Arthur Smith’s wide-zone scheme, and now Mike McCarthy is a more pro-style, downhill, gap-scheme.” That change could be particularly important for a young offensive line that was beginning to develop familiarity with Smith’s system. McCarthy, who is also calling the plays in Pittsburgh, has brought a different offensive philosophy with him, including a greater emphasis on power/gap concepts and physicality up front. The Steelers have also undergone considerable personnel changes along the line. Zach Frazier remains the anchor at center after establishing himself as one of the league’s better young centers. Troy Fautanu is taking over at left tackle, while Mason McCormick has moved to left guard. Rookie Max Iheanachor is also in the mix on the right side, but Dylan Cook will likely start the season at right tackle. The Steelers recently traded former first-round pick Broderick Jones to the Dallas Cowboys, further changing the complexion of the unit heading into the regular season. That leaves Pittsburgh with a group featuring plenty of youth and athleticism, but also a significant amount of responsibility in a new system. Shipley believes that transition could expose the Steelers, particularly if the offensive line struggles to generate the necessary movement in a more physical scheme. “I think they struggled handling that a little bit,” he said. There are reasons for optimism, however. The Steelers have spent plenty of draft capital in the group in recent seasons, with Frazier and Fautanu establishing themselves as foundational players for the future. Still, Shipley’s pessimism highlights one of the biggest questions surrounding Pittsburgh entering the McCarthy era: Can a young offensive line quickly adjust to a completely different offensive identity? The group’s rough preseason didn’t do much to alleviate those concerns. With Aaron Rodgers entering the season behind center and Pittsburgh hoping to compete immediately, the answer could have a major impact on how successful the new-look offense becomes.

title: Steelers QB watch: Five draft-eligible passers to watch Saturday
summary: College football Week 1 is upon us, and for the NFL Draft nerds, there are plenty of potential Steelers storylines to be found in Labor Day weekend’s slate of games. Notably, at the quarterback position. With Aaron Rodgers publicly announcing that he plans to retire after the 2026 season, quarterback remains a clear top need […]
full_text: Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker throws a pass during an Oklahoma State University Cowboys football spring practice in Stillwater, Wednesday, April 1, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co College football Week 1 is upon us, and for the NFL Draft nerds, there are plenty of potential Steelers storylines to be found in Labor Day weekend’s slate of games. Notably, at the quarterback position. With Aaron Rodgers publicly announcing that he plans to retire after the 2026 season, quarterback remains a clear top need for the Steelers ahead of the upcoming offseason. And yes, 2026 third-rounder Drew Allar should be considered an option for the team in 2027, but he’s only appeared in three preseason games in his young NFL career thus far. That means the Pittsburgh front office will still absolutely be doing its homework this college season on prospects playing football’s most important position — and if you’re interested, you can certainly do the same. If you’re sitting down to watch some football this Saturday, here are five games (and quarterbacks of interest) at different time slots. To keep things somewhat interesting, I’m leaving the two big names at the position, Texas’ Arch Manning and Oregon’s Dante Moore, off this list. Odds are the Steelers won’t ever be in the running for either player, and even if they are, you probably already know quite a bit about them. Also, keep in mind that top quarterback prospects such as USC’s Jayden Maiava and Miami’s Darian Mensah already played this week. That’s a lot of intro. Let’s name some quarterbacks. Josh Hoover, Indiana (Noon EST vs. North Texas) Hoover, a TCU transfer, has big shoes to fill at Indiana, following up a legendary 2025 season from the NFL’s most recent No. 1 overall pick, Fernando Mendoza. However, Hoover is a talented player in his own right, and he’s expected to take a leap under the coaching of Curt Cignetti in a burgeoning Indiana football program. Summer scouting reports have praised Hoover’s smooth mechanics, pocket mobility and processing, but concerns remain about if he has high-end NFL tools, and the 13 interceptions he threw in 2025. Pinpoint placement from Josh Hoover right here from a moving platform, whew. pic.twitter.com/2jJMNLNyno https://t.co/qg7TDdxez5 — Nick Martin (@themicknartin) September 17, 2025 At the very least, tune in to watch an Indiana team loaded with other NFL prospects, including offensive tackle Carter Smith and wide receivers Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh. Josh Hoover basics: Listed at 6’2, 205 pounds; fifth-year senior; 3,472 passing yards, 29 passing touchdowns and 13 interceptions in 2025 for TCU Julian Sayin, Ohio State (12:30 p.m. EST vs. Ball State) Sayin has some similarities to Hoover in that both are expected to be piloting high-end offenses in 2026 and thus cement themselves in the upper echelon of college quarterbacks — but when it comes to NFL chances, their talent profiles come with some legitimate questions. Analysts have described Sayin as a capable point guard on offense with plus accuracy and touch as well as a knack for play action. Detractors include a lack of ideal NFL size and good, not great arm strength, although Sayin is certainly able to make some highlight throws. I have watched this 50000000 times and I still…. WHAT? pic.twitter.com/CEh5pASvPH — Anand Nanduri (@NanduriNFL) November 4, 2025 The narrative with Sayin entering the fall is if he can further his NFL Draft profile by standing out on a team full of standouts. It’ll be hard not to be overshadowed by Jeremiah Smith, who enters 2026 as Sayin’s top target and arguably the top wide receiver in college football. Julian Sayin basics: Listed at 6’1, 214 pounds; junior; 3,610 passing yards, 32 touchdowns and eight interceptions in 2025 for Ohio State LaNorris Sellers, South Carolina (12:45 p.m. EST vs. Kent State) Sellers might be the most physically gifted quarterback in the upcoming draft class, and his decision to return to school for the 2026 season was a move analysts hoped would result in further refinement of his game before hitting the NFL stage. Sellers has typical NFL size for the position, rushing ability with both speed and power, and plus arm strength. The concerns, as you might expect, have to do with the rawness in his game in aspects such as processing and decision-making. back-to-back plays that show the highs of LaNorris Sellers. Drifts in the pocket and nails the throw to convert on 4th & long (while handling the pre-snap operation, too). Next play runs in for a TD on a heroic effort, but it gets called back because of a penalty. pic.twitter.com/1fG47AXjwl — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) October 29, 2025 Even if Sellers can’t fully realize his potential in 2026, expect NFL teams to remain highly interested. In a world where every quarterback-needy team is trying to replicate the Josh Allen success story, Sellers will remain a name to watch. LaNorris Sellers basics: Listed at 6’3, 238 pounds; redshirt junior; 2,437 passing yards, 13 passing touchdowns, eight interceptions in 2025 for South Carolina. Drew Mestemaker, Oklahoma State (3:45 p.m. EST vs. Tulsa) A North Texas transfer, Mestemaker hopes to make the jump to Power Four football in 2026, and possibly emerge as one of the top draft-eligible quarterbacks in the process. Mestemaker is a tall, lanky prospect with a big arm that pops on-screen, as well as an unorthodox throwing motion. He made all sorts of highlight throws last year, but one of the bigger questions entering this season is if his sometimes-zany playing style can survive at a higher level of the sport. Drew Mestemaker belongs in some outrageous convos pic.twitter.com/HLDvR9vZ5a — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) April 26, 2026 Mestemaker has clear high-end traits, but his game is still somewhat raw, and he’d likely need to bulk up a bit for the NFL level. He’s a favorite among draft nerds to break out in 2026, but there’s also an expectation that he might return to school instead of declaring in 2027. Drew Mestemaker basics: Listed at 6’3, 215 pounds; redshirt sophomore; 4,379 passing yards, 34 passing touchdowns and nine interceptions in 2025 for North Texas. CJ Carr, Notre Dame (7:30 p.m. EST vs. Wisconsin) Carr has been the beneficiary of plenty of offseason hype entering 2026, now considered one of the favorites for the 2026 Heisman Trophy after a promising 2025 campaign. Carr fits a similar mold to the likes of Sayin and Hoover: regarded for football smarts, rhythm and accuracy despite not many rave reviews about arm talent or high-end mobility. But now, without the star power of Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price in the Fighting Irish backfield, Carr has a chance to really emerge as the focal point of the Notre Dame offense. CJ Carr | QB | Notre Dame | 6-3, 210 Efficient and poised rhythm-based distributor that continued to grow as the season progressed. Polished mechanics and has experience with exhausting progressions. pic.twitter.com/CKPL6DLBFs — Jordan Reid (@Jordan_Reid) June 28, 2026 While he doesn’t look huge on the screen, Carr brings solid NFL size to the table. Scouting reports also like to note his strong football bloodlines as the grandson of College Football Hall of Fame coach Lloyd Carr. CJ Carr basics: Listed at 6’2, 215 pounds; junior; 2,741 passing yards, 24 passing touchdowns and six interceptions in 2025 for Notre Dame .

full_text: Aug 23, 2025; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Seattle Seahawks safety D'Anthony Bell (23) during the game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. summary: The 2026 season is upon us! How will the Seahawks do to start the season? […]
full_text: The 2026 season is upon us! Seattle Seahawks regular season football is close at hand, and the Super Bowl banner reveal will feel so sweet as the Seahawks will face the New England Patriots in a Super Bowl rematch at home in Lumen Field September 9th. How will the Seahawks do to start the season? Without seeing how the 2026 team as a whole play together in a game, especially the offense with a new lead running back and new offensive coordinator, it is hard to say. The only data we have for both of these teams are from 2025, and since the teams as a whole are mostly the same, we will use the entirety of the 2025 regular season and playoffs to try to predict this first game. With that said, we will do our best, as we dive into the Week 1 matchup! What better way to kick off a new season than with a Super Bowl rematch? 😮‍💨 NEvsSEA – Wednesday, Sept. 9 at 8:20pm ET on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/HIM6lIovED — NFL (@NFL) September 2, 2026 The Seahawks The Seahawks in 2025 were a dominant force. In 2025, they went 17-3 overall capping off the season with that Super Bowl win, and they topped the overall DVOA rankings. They won 85 percent of their games. That is a great percentage, and since the team is mostly the same, I expect similar results this season. With that, they scored an average of 29 points per game with the 10th ranked DVOA on offense, while allowing a league-low 17 points per game . That is a difference of 12 points per game, and no team had a greater point differential than the Seahawks. The Super Bowl champions only allowed an average three to four scores per game, including one shut out against the Minnesota Vikings in 2025. That is a stalwart defense worthy of its number one finish by FTN’s DVOA last season . The Patriots Easy schedule or not in 2025, the Patriots still were a good team analytically. They ended the season 16-4 , playoffs included, and the ninth best team by DVOA. That is an 80 percent win rate, and one many teams wish they had. They averaged 28 points per game and ranked 3rd in DVOA, and allowing 19 points against, a difference of nine points . They allowed an average of four to five scores per game, and were only the 23rd ranked defense per DVOA. Seahawks vs. Patriots score prediction If you were to average out the points the Seahawks scored (29) and the points the Patriots allowed (19) you would come out to 24 points for the Seahawks. For the Patriots, if you averaged they points they scored (28) and the points the Seahawks allowed (17), you come out to 23 points. With that, the Seahawks would be ahead with 24 points to the Patriots 23. Seahawks look to repeat and be the victors of this matchup. Due to that, there is more math to be had. Seahawks on average scored 12 more points than their opponents, so after subtracting that from the Seahawks score to have that 12 point difference, you get an end result of Seahawks 24 Patriots 12 . In conclusion With it being a home game, having the fans being that 12th Man in the stands cheering them on, I fully expect the Seahawks to win the game. The 24-12 victory is what I am locking in. As the season progresses, I will be using 2026 data to make score predictions. I will be having a weekly show over on The Hawks Eye Podcast called “Eye on the Numbers” every Wednesday at 6:30 PM PST starting September 16th were I will be going more in depth on game predictions for the Seahawks. Hope to see you there! What’s your early score prediction for Seahawks vs. Patriots, the rematch? Give us your picks in the comments section and stick around for more previews over the next few days! In hindsight, it was always a puzzling decision to keep Willis over rookie undrafted free agent Bryson Eason.
